title: The agent's only output channel is one giant Write, so output size is unbounded and uncheckpointed
description: The quantify agent's toolset is `Read, Glob, Write` and its output contract is a single file at a single path, so a whole department's delta must be emitted as one atomic tool call. That call is bounded by the model's 64,000-token per-message output cap, which nothing in the playbook, spec or prompt ever mentions. Every crash in the run reduces to this: the first full-mode dispatch, three of the eight rescue passes' fix rounds, and every fix round that had to re-emit an entire file to change ten strings. A crash loses 100% of the work because there is no partial file, no append, no per-entry sink and no checkpoint.
evidence: quantify.md:5 `tools: Read, Glob, Write`; quantify.md output contract 'write {run_dir}/facts-delta.json'. First dispatch agent-ad4582d793bae7b62: 17:34:35→18:21:16, 79 Read calls, ZERO Write calls, four consecutive attempts ending 'API Error: Claude's response exceeded the 64000 output token maximum'. The delta the same inputs eventually produced is 1,013,794 B / 485 entries ≈ 440K output tokens, ~7× the cap. Store average is 1,809 B ≈ 517 output tokens per entry, so the cap is hit at ~124 entries; parts B3 (100 entries/193,160 B), B6 (80/182,283 B), B4 (81/164,816 B) were sized above it. B3's fix round: four attempts 21:36:15→22:12:55 (9m17s, 9m11s, 9m16s, 8m56s), zero bytes written; B6 the same, 38.6 min and ~1.1M cache-creation tokens for nothing. B1's fix rewrote 102,653 B (47,736 output tokens) to change 10 entries by +842 chars.
root_cause: No output budget exists at any layer: the playbook treats 'a department' as one unit of work regardless of estate size, nothing estimates output volume before dispatch, and the Write-only toolset (chosen for INV-1 safety) forbids incremental emission. ADR 0015 explicitly assumed the opposite ('the pipeline emits many small turns, not one huge output') and the Opus-5 migration plan listed large-single-response truncation as open risk #1 and never mitigated it.
sources: full-mode transcript audit, B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B7, B8, coordinator, runtime/harness, plan-vs-implementation, input-shape

verdict.reason:
Tried to refute; every load-bearing piece of evidence reproduced, and I found two extra pieces that strengthen it. Three details in the write-up are wrong (crash count, part sizing, per-entry arithmetic, and the nature of the cap).

CONFIRMED — mechanism.
- data-repo/.claude/agents/quantify.md:5 `tools: Read, Glob, Write`; line 248 "For **full** and **targeted** mode: write `{run_dir}/facts-delta.json`" — one path, whole-file writes only.
- Deliberate, not accidental: spec 2026-08-29-quantitative-facts-design.md:1426 "`model: claude-opus-5[1m]`, `tools: Read, Glob, Write` — no Bash, no ids, no hashing" (QF-19).
- NEW, stronger than the frontmatter: two agents actually tried to emit incrementally and were refused. B6 (agent-a6bcbaa3c3e516146) at 20:33:37 Tehran issued `Edit facts-delta-B6.json` appending 13,136 chars of new entries onto `"\n]\n}\n"`; B8 (agent-ac302b9fded70ff8d) at 21:30:09 issued a 55-char Edit. Both got `<tool_use_error>Error: No such tool available: Edit. Edit is disabled for this session, in subagents as well as here.</tool_use_error>`. So the block is a session-wide harness setting, not only the agent's `tools:` line — patching the frontmatter alone would not restore append. B6 then re-emitted the whole file (104,510 chars).

CONFIRMED — the crashes.
- First dispatch agent-ad4582d793bae7b62: 14:04:35→14:51:16Z = 17:34:35→18:21:16 Tehran, 46m41s. 79 tool calls (78 Read + 1 Glob — the write-up says "79 Read"), ZERO Write. Tail: 14:14:05 "I have the full picture. Writing the delta." then four assistant turns at 14:21:12, 14:31:10, 14:41:29, 14:51:16, the last carrying `API Error: Claude's response exceeded the 64000 output token maximum.` 100% of 47 min lost, no partial file.
- B3 fix round (agent-af32a299db7aa1c17): fix prompt 21:34:48, first attempt starts 21:36:15, then 21:45:32 (+9m17s), 21:54:43 (+9m11s), 22:03:59 (+9m16s), 22:12:55 (+8m56s) = API error. Zero bytes written. 1,282,856 cache-creation tokens after the fix prompt. Exactly as claimed.
- B6 fix round (agent-a6bcbaa3c3e516146): 21:39:07→22:17:41 = 38m34s, four attempts (+8m49, +10m04, +9m52, +9m49), API error, zero bytes. cache_creation on the three completed attempts = 368,681+368,743+368,805 = 1,106,229 ≈ "~1.1M". Exactly as claimed.
- Only 3 API-error events exist in the whole run: `grep -c isApiErrorMessage` = 1 in each of ad4582 / af32a2 / a6bcba, 0 in the other six subagents and 0 in the coordinator ffa1efdd…jsonl.
- B1 fix (agent-ab4a169f8d48fbaf3): write #1 86,965 chars / 102,653 UTF-8 B; write #2 87,807 chars / 103,845 B at output_tokens=47,736. Diffing the two JSON payloads: 67 entries both sides, 10 entries changed, 0 added, 0 removed, +834 chars on the changed entries (+842 whole file). Confirmed — a 103.8 KB re-emission for a 10-string edit.

CONFIRMED — root cause.
- Zero hits for `64000|64,000|64k|output token|max_output|token limit|budget` in data-repo/.claude/skills/quantify/SKILL.md, data-repo/.claude/agents/quantify.md, and the spec. Nothing anywhere mentions the cap.
- SKILL.md Stage 3 dispatches exactly one `quantify` full-mode Task per department, listing every dump/script/image/transcript, with no size estimate or partition rule. Stage 4's failure path is "re-dispatch `quantify` (mode `full`, same inputs) with the stderr error appended" — i.e. a full re-emission to fix any error, which is precisely what killed B3 and B6.
- ADR 0015 (docs/decisions/0015-control-bot-1m-context-window.md:88-89) verbatim: "`maxOutputTokens` for the variant is **64000** (unchanged concern — the pipeline emits many small turns, not one huge output)."
- Migration plan 2026-07-24-opus-5-1m-model-migration.md:169-171 open risk #1: "`maxOutputTokens` drops 64000 → 32000 on Opus 5 … Large `extract`/`merge` outputs could truncate … options are to stay on 4.8, or investigate a Claude-Code max-output override." No override exists: `grep -rn MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` over both repos and ~/.claude/settings.json returns nothing.

WRONG IN THE WRITE-UP (all corrected below):
1. "the model's 64,000-token per-message output cap" — it is Claude Code's configurable `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS`, named in the error text itself and recorded as harness `maxOutputTokens: 64000` in ADR 0015:70. Unset everywhere. Matters: one env var is a partial mitigation the write-up's framing rules out.
2. "three of the eight rescue passes' fix rounds" crashed — only two did (B3, B6). Total crash events in the run = 3 (first dispatch + those two). Fix rounds for B1, B2, B4, B8 all completed.
3. "parts B3 (100 entries/193,160 B), B6 (80/182,283 B), B4 (81/164,816 B) were sized above it" — false; each of those was emitted in ONE successful Write. Those on-disk byte figures are the coordinator's post-processed files (it ran 50 python/jq passes over parts/); the agents' actual Write payloads were B3 107,613 chars, B6 104,510, B4 103,506, all just UNDER the ceiling. The real point is the opposite and worse: the successful writes sat at ~95-100% of the cap with no headroom, so any rewrite that grew by a few percent died.
4. Per-entry arithmetic — "store average is 1,809 B ≈ 517 output tokens/entry → cap at ~124 entries". 1,809 is chars/entry in the delta (877,739 chars / 485 = 1,810); bytes/entry is 2,090 in the delta and 2,686 in the store (1,305,221 B / 486 entries across facts/{items,records,rules,notes,measurements}.json). Measured token rate from B1 (87,807 chars = 47,736 output tokens) is 1.84 chars/token and 712 tokens/entry, so the practical ceiling is ~115,000 chars ≈ ~90 entries, not 124. The full 877,739-char delta ≈ 490K output tokens ≈ 7.6× the cap (claim said 440K / 7×).
5. "A crash loses 100% of the work" — true for the first dispatch (zero Writes). For B3/B6 the earlier part file survived on disk, so it was 100% of the fix attempt. Note the escape route that actually worked: at 22:22:18 the coordinator applied the mechanical fixes itself in python and asked B6 for only the 64 remaining rule entries, which it emitted first try (81,623 chars) — narrowing the write is a proven fix.

Severity high is right: ~2h07m of pure wall-clock loss (47 + 38 + 42 min) plus ~4.3M cache-creation tokens on the two dead fix rounds, and it is the direct cause of the 8-way split (coordinator ffa1efdd made 9 Agent dispatches and 7 SendMessage fix rounds).
verdict.corrected: The quantify agent's only output channel is a single whole-file Write to one path, so a department's delta must be emitted as one atomic tool call bounded by Claude Code's configurable `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS` (default 64,000; no override is set anywhere in either repo or ~/.claude/settings.json), and nothing in the playbook, the agent prompt or the spec mentions that budget. Empirically the ceiling is ~1.84 chars per output token → ~115,000 chars ≈ ~90 entries of this delta; the whole cooking delta is 877,739 chars ≈ 490K output tokens, ~7.6× the cap. All three crashes in the run are this: the first full-mode dispatch (agent-ad4582d, 17:34:35→18:21:16 Tehran, 79 tool calls, zero Writes, four ~10-min emission attempts ending in the 64000 error), B3's fix round (four attempts 21:36:15→22:12:55, zero bytes, 1.28M cache-creation tokens) and B6's fix round (38m34s, four attempts, ~1.1M cache-creation tokens) — two of eight rescue passes, not three. The parts that succeeded were not oversized; they sat at 87K-108K chars, i.e. 95-100% of the cap with no headroom, which is why any rewrite that grew died while B4's and B1's, which did not, survived. Every fix round re-emitted a whole file to change a handful of strings: B1's rewrote 103,845 B at 47,736 output tokens to alter 10 of 67 entries by +842 chars — mandated by SKILL.md Stage 4, whose only failure path is "re-dispatch `quantify` (mode `full`, same inputs)". A crash loses the entire emission because there is no partial file, no append and no checkpoint: B6 and B8 both tried an incremental `Edit` append and were refused with "Edit is disabled for this session, in subagents as well as here" — a harness-level block, not just the agent's `tools:` line. Root cause as stated is correct: no output budget exists at any layer, Stage 3 dispatches one agent per department regardless of estate size, nothing estimates output volume before dispatch, ADR 0015:88 explicitly assumed the opposite ("the pipeline emits many small turns, not one huge output"), and the Opus-5 migration plan's open risk #1 (large-response truncation) was never mitigated. Severity high: ~2h07m wall clock and ~4.3M cache-creation tokens lost, and it forced the 8-way sequential split. The one demonstrated escape is narrowing the write — after the coordinator applied B6's mechanical fixes itself in python and asked only for the 64 remaining rule entries, the agent emitted them first try.

title: Eight independent passes ran strictly sequentially: 3h06m where the parallel critical path was 43m
description: All nine Agent dispatches used the blocking form with `run_in_background:false`, so the eight rescue passes ran one after another even though they covered disjoint workbook sets. Two minutes after the last pass finished, the same coordinator resumed six fix agents in parallel — so it could parallelise and chose not to. Each finished batch then sat idle for hours with its ~250-300K-token context alive, blowing the 5-minute ephemeral cache TTL at both ends.
evidence: Pass windows: B1 14m32s, B2 11m04s, B3 25m25s, B4 43m19s, B5 13m06s, B6 38m41s, B7 14m17s, B8 22m10s — phase total 3h06m27s. Fully parallel = 43m19s (saves 2h23m); three waves = 1h20m (saves 1h46m). B1 idle 174.4 min between finishing (18:39:52) and its fix message (21:34:13); B3 idle 2h18m14s; B4 idle 93.9 min then re-created a ~300K context at write price (cache_creation 301,695 / 322,899 / 384,180 with cache_read 10,699). ADR 0011 had already verified bounded parallel batches of 4 on this exact 2-CPU server (11 processes in 3 batches, one ~16-min turn).
root_cause: The playbook says 'wait for it to complete' for its single Stage-3 Task and says nothing about many; the coordinator generalised the blocking wait to eight. The facts pipeline was written as a greenfield sibling of process-voice and never inherited its operational ADRs (0003/0005/0006/0007/0011).
sources: coordinator, B1, B2, B3, B4, B6, B7, runtime/harness

verdict.reason:
VERIFIED (all numbers reproduce exactly)

Dispatch structure — coordinator transcript /home/lili/.claude/projects/-home-lili-Desktop-DriveD-work-Moshtaghi-Inja-food-process-process-dev-data-repo/ffa1efdd-cf44-4caa-b4e3-9b3853970a43.jsonl: 9 tool_use of name `Agent` (not `Task`), every one with `run_in_background: false`, and — checked block-by-block — every one is the ONLY tool_use block in its assistant message (timestamps 14:04:32, 14:55:20, 15:10:26, 15:22:03, 15:47:58, 16:31:55, 16:45:42, 17:24:55, 17:39:37 UTC).

Durations (tool_use → tool_result, Tehran): full-mode 17:34:32→18:21:16 = 46m44s (crash, max_output_tokens); B1 18:25:20→18:39:52 = 14m32s; B2 18:40:26→18:51:30 = 11m04s; B3 18:52:03→19:17:28 = 25m25s; B4 19:17:58→20:01:17 = 43m19s; B5 20:01:55→20:15:01 = 13m06s; B6 20:15:42→20:54:23 = 38m41s; B7 20:54:55→21:09:12 = 14m17s; B8 21:09:37→21:31:47 = 22m10s. Window B1-start→B8-end = 3h06m27s. All eight figures in the claim are exact.

Parallel resume confirmed: 6 SendMessage fix messages at 21:34:10, 21:34:25, 21:34:46, 21:35:09, 21:35:27, 21:35:48 (first is 2m23s after B8 returned), each returning in <4s, and the six subagent transcripts show genuinely overlapping activity: B1 21:34:13→21:41:27, B2 21:34:27→21:40:09, B3 21:34:48→22:12:55, B4 21:35:12→21:56:10, B6 21:35:29→22:31:03, B8 21:35:49→21:44:17. Six concurrent subagents worked fine in this harness on this host.

Idle: B1 18:39:50→21:34:13 = 174.4 min (exact match); B4 20:01:15→21:35:12 = 93.9 min (exact); B3 19:17:25→21:34:48 = 137.4 min (claim said 2h18m14s = 138.2 min, off ~50s). B4 cache usage exact: 21:35:18 cc=301,695 cr=10,699; 21:46:12 cc=322,899 cr=10,699; 21:56:10 cc=384,180 cr=10,699.

ADR 0011 exists (code-repo/docs/decisions/0011-extract-bounded-parallel-batch-of-4.md), supersedes 0003, verified 11 processes in 3 batches (4+4+3) in one ~16-min turn. quantify/SKILL.md Stage 3 says exactly "Wait for it to complete" for its single Task; grep of SKILL.md and .claude/agents/quantify.md for parallel|run_in_background|batch found nothing.

WHAT IS WRONG

1. "Eight INDEPENDENT passes … covered disjoint workbook sets" — the workbook sets were disjoint, the passes were not independent. Every prompt from B2 on orders the agent to read the earlier part files and (a) not re-mint a key an earlier part minted, (b) `ref` earlier parts' temp ids directly. The chain was actually used: counting T-Nxxx ids per part file, B3 carries 85 refs into B1's 1000-block, B4 44 into B1's, B5 refs B1(20)/B3(33)/B4(2), B7 refs B2(17)/B3(34)/B6(4), B8 refs B1(39)/B3(8)/B4(21). B6's own return message states it could not bind four «مصرف واقعی» rules because "the records in question are the Table_SalesData_* mirrors, which batch 7 creates — their temp ids and field keys are not knowable here". And the engine makes the chain load-bearing: engine/merge_facts/apply.py:351 emits "duplicate natural key {key} in delta" as a hard content error, so two parallel passes both minting e.g. `item_##NN` would have failed the apply. Consequence: "fully parallel = 43m19s, saves 2h23m" is not reachable without redesigning key minting/dedup. Only the "three waves ≈ 1h20m" figure is defensible (B1 alone 14.5m → B2/B3/B4/B6 43.3m → B5/B7/B8 22.2m = 80.0m), i.e. ~1h46m saved, and even that needs B1's conventions hoisted into a shared preamble.

2. The named mechanism is wrong. `run_in_background:false` did not serialise them — one Agent block per assistant message did. ADR 0011's own parallel form is several BLOCKING Agent blocks in one message; ADR 0006 (CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_BACKGROUND_TASKS=1) deliberately disables background deferral for this pipeline's deployed path. So "should have set run_in_background:true" is the wrong prescription.

3. "on this exact 2-CPU server" is false for this run. This run was on the dev box: nproc=12, 15 GB RAM, paths under /home/lili/Desktop/. The 2-CPU/3.7 GB box in ADR 0006/0011 is the control-bot server. (The error favours the claim — this host had more headroom, and 6-way concurrency demonstrably ran on it.)

4. "blowing the 5-minute cache TTL at both ends" is true at the resume boundary but not exclusive to idling: B4 already paid two full cache re-creations INSIDE its own pass (19:36:18 cc=220,629 cr=0; 20:01:15 cc=308,841 cr=0) from long in-pass gaps.

5. Root cause is half right. The coordinator did not merely generalise the blocking wait: at 18:24:59 it stated the choice — «حجم داده‌ها از ظرفیت یک پاس عبور کرد؛ استخراج را به چند پاس پشت‌سرهم می‌شکنم» ("…I'll break extraction into several BACK-TO-BACK passes") — then built cross-pass key reuse on top of that choice, which foreclosed parallelism. The playbook-silence and ADR-non-inheritance halves are confirmed.

SEVERITY: medium, not high. Real saving ~1h46m not 2h23m; capturing it needs a dependency redesign (shared conventions preamble + merge-time key dedup), not a flag; and parallelism would have prevented none of the failures — both crashes (full mode, and the B3/B6 fix rounds) were max_output_tokens.
verdict.corrected: Eight chained passes ran strictly sequentially: 3h06m27s where a dependency-aware three-wave schedule was ~1h20m (saving ~1h46m). The coordinator issued nine `Agent` dispatches each as the sole tool_use block in its own message, which is what serialised them (not `run_in_background:false` — ADR 0011's parallel form is several blocking Agent blocks in ONE message, and ADR 0006 disables background deferral for this pipeline). The passes covered disjoint workbook sets but were NOT independent: every prompt from B2 on required reading the earlier part files to avoid re-minting keys and to `ref` earlier temp ids, and the chain was really used (B3 refs 85 B1 temp ids, B8 refs B1/B3/B4, B6 explicitly could not bind four rules because B7 had not run) — a requirement the engine enforces, since merge_facts/apply.py:351 rejects a duplicate natural key in the concatenated delta. So full parallelism (43m) was unreachable without also hoisting the naming/granularity conventions into a shared preamble and moving dedup to merge time. Two minutes after B8 the same coordinator resumed six fix agents that ran genuinely concurrently (21:34:13–22:31:03, overlapping windows), proving the harness and host support parallelism — the host being the 12-CPU dev box, not the 2-CPU control-bot server ADR 0011 was verified on. Idle cost is real: B1 sat 174.4 min, B3 137.4 min, B4 93.9 min, and B4's resume re-created its context at write price (cache_creation 301,695 / 322,899 / 384,180 against cache_read 10,699) — though B4 had already eaten two full cache re-creations inside its own pass from long in-pass gaps. Root cause: the coordinator explicitly chose back-to-back passes («به چند پاس پشت‌سرهم می‌شکنم», 18:24:59) and then made them mutually dependent; the playbook says only "Wait for it to complete" for a single Stage-3 Task and nothing about many, and the facts pipeline inherited none of process-voice's operational ADRs (0003/0011). Severity: medium — the recoverable time is ~1h46m, the fix is a redesign rather than a flag, and parallelism would not have prevented either crash (both were max_output_tokens).

title: Each pass was ordered to read all its predecessors, manufacturing a serial dependency and propagating errors between branches
description: Every batch dispatch told the agent to read the earlier parts first and to 'keep B1's conventions', which is what forced the sequential schedule and made an unvalidated sibling output the authoritative style guide. B1's malformed process source ref (`"ref": "cooking-030"` instead of the file path) was copied verbatim into B2 and onward before anyone had validated B1. B4's wrong `name`-keyed rule members were explicitly mirrored by B6 by instruction, producing two identical 358-error profiles. The reading cost more context than the work: B2 spent ~146K input tokens on the write turn, most of it a sibling batch's output, against 42,743 bytes of actual batch source material.
evidence: B2 dispatch 'Keep B1's other conventions'; B6 dispatch '**Follow B4's granularity decision exactly**', 'Mirror B4's key shapes', 'Consistency between the two branches matters more than either choice alone'. Coordinator to B6 21:35:29: 'Your error profile is identical to part B4's, class for class and count for count.' errs_B2.txt errors 1-9 and 14 are all the copied `ref` bug. B8 dispatch: 'Read all seven previous passes first' — the seven parts total ~950 KB against a 25K-token Read cap, so B8 read only three, partially. B1 also handed B2 the '149' note as the canonical note shape.
root_cause: Convention sharing was implemented as file-reading between passes rather than as a conventions block in every prompt or a one-time key-map pass; and no batch was validated before the next one read it, so one formatting error was multiplied by eight. Temp ids are per-delta and file-local, which additionally forces the order.
sources: B2, B3, B4, B6, B7, B8, coordinator

verdict.reason: P-03 is real and every load-bearing piece of evidence reproduces; three secondary claims are wrong and the root cause is incomplete. (5) B8's read failure reproduces exactly: it read only B1 (3 chunks, ~50.7K tok), B4 (partial, after four 25K-cap rejections; "File content (59429 tokens) exceeds maximum allowed tokens (25000)") and B3 (partial, 46,906 tok file); it never opened B2, B5, B6 or B7. The first validate in the whole coordinator session is at 21:32:41, after all eight finished. (8) Aggregate cost, measured as per-turn context growth up to each batch's first Write, excluding self-file reads: sibling-part reads = 613,998 tokens vs 822,798 for everything else (which includes ~137K of base prompts, so ~686K of actual own-source reading). Sibling reading exceeded own-source reading in B5 (103,689 vs ~76.5K), B7 (88,611 vs ~65K) and B8 (146,937 vs ~52K). REFUTED SUB-CLAIMS: (a) "most of it a sibling batch's output" — false. B1 cost B2 54,980 tokens = 38% of the 145,848-token write turn; the rest was 30,091 for its own dumps, 33,615 for cooking-030/032, 8,243 manifest, 17,359 base. B1 was the largest single read and 1.8x the pass's own dump material, but not a majority. (b) "B1 also handed B2 the '149' note as the canonical note shape" — false. B1's junk note kanter__mojudi__comment_149 {"text":"149","meaning":null} propagated nowhere: B2's one note is a substantive gloss with `meaning` filled and no `text`, and B3-B7 emitted zero notes (B8's 20 are transcript-derived). (d) "B4's wrong `name`-keyed rule members" mislabels the defect: the two families are undeclared identifiers in rule `expr` (260) and record `rows[]` members not matching `fields[]` (74) plus primaryKey members (4). ROOT CAUSE INCOMPLETE: the serial dependency is not purely manufactured by the prompt wording. Two engine facts make it real once you concatenate: `apply.py:362` builds `by_temp = {e["id"]: e for e in entries}` so temp ids resolve only inside one delta file (schema `ref` pattern is `^(F-[0-9]{5}|T-[0-9]+)$` — a natural key is not a legal ref target), and `apply.py:343-352` rejects "duplicate natural key … in delta", so two parallel batches both minting `item_74` would have failed apply outright (B2 minted 0 items precisely because it reused B1's 52). The upstream choice is the playbook's one-delta-per-run shape, which the coordinator honoured by concatenating eight parts; the "read your predecessors" wording is the mechanism that choice forced, not the origin. Note also that what the dependency actually needed was B1's 52 item keys (~2KB), not its 142,501-byte file — which is exactly the key-map pass the stated root cause proposes.
verdict.corrected: Each pass was ordered to read all its predecessors' delta files, which forced a strictly serial schedule and propagated unvalidated errors between branches. Every dispatch from B2 on carried a "read the previous pass(es) first" instruction plus explicit convention-inheritance wording ("Keep B1's other conventions"; for B6, "Follow B4's granularity decision exactly", "Mirror B4's key shapes", "Consistency between the two branches matters more than either choice alone"), making an unvalidated sibling output the authoritative style guide. B1's malformed process-type source ref (`"ref": "cooking-030"` where the engine requires the path ending `cooking-030.json`) was copied byte-for-byte — ref, node and quote — into B2's first write and reappears in B4, B6 and B8 (34 instances across five of eight parts; errs_B2.txt lines 1-9 and 14). B8 stated it had copied the shape "verbatim from B1". The prompt was silent on this at run time — quantify.md's "ref is a FILE PATH, never an identifier" rule was added four days later (commit 03790ad, 2026-09-06). B6 was instructed to mirror B4 and read B4 as its first action (~62K tokens before opening its own workbook); the two parts' validation errors are an identical multiset — 358 lines each, zero difference after stripping temp ids, down to identifier names — even though the dispatch itself records the twin workbooks as non-identical (62/55/29/25 vs 62/54/29/25 formulas). No part was ever validated before the next one read it, and could not have been: the quantify agent's tool list is Read/Glob/Write with no Bash, and the playbook's only `validate facts-delta` is a Stage-4 whole-delta call, first run at 21:32:41 after all eight passes finished. The reading was the larger half of the run's input: 613,998 tokens spent on sibling part files against ~686K on the passes' own sources, and it exceeded own-source reading outright in B5, B7 and B8. It also did not work at scale — B8 was told to read all seven predecessors (954,102 bytes) against a 25,000-token Read cap and got through only B1, plus partial B4 and B3, never opening B2, B5, B6 or B7. Two claims in the original statement do not hold: B1 was 54,980 tokens, 38% — not "most" — of B2's 145,848-token write turn (though still 1.8x the 42,743 bytes of dumps that pass existed to read), and B1's junk "149" note propagated nowhere, B2's only note being a substantive gloss of a different shape. The root cause is convention-sharing implemented as file-reading plus no per-batch validation gate, but the serial dependency was not purely manufactured by the wording: it follows from concatenating eight parts into ONE delta, where `apply` resolves temp ids only within a single file (a natural key is not a legal ref target) and rejects duplicate natural keys inside one delta — so parallel passes minting the same item would have failed apply. The fix is therefore three-part: hoist conventions into every prompt instead of a sibling file, hand each pass a small key map (B2 needed B1's 52 item keys, ~2KB, not its 142KB file) or let each batch apply as its own delta, and validate each part before the next one is dispatched.

title: Validation ran once, after everything, 2h53m after the first part returned: 2,068 errors accumulated
description: The playbook's Stage 4 validates a single concatenated delta and the improvised eight-way split never added a per-part gate, so eight agents independently repeated the same mistakes with no feedback. A 30-second validate after B1 would have corrected the process-ref convention and the `name`-vs-`key` convention for the remaining seven passes. Instead the errors surfaced as one 148 KB / 2,069-line pile that the coordinator had to triage in bash before it could route anything.
evidence: First `validate facts-delta` at 21:32:41, 2h52m49s after B1 returned at 18:39:52. Per batch: B1 11, B2 21, B3 1306, B4 358, B5 0, B6 358, B7 0, B8 12, no-key 2 = 2,068. Classes: 1086 'reference row missing declared field', 525 'expr identifier not declared', 355 'row member is not a declared field', 34 processes[] link, 21 constant-output. B4 and B6 produced 358 identical errors each because B6 was told to mirror B4. Output was too large to return inline ('Output too large (148KB). Full output saved to …').
root_cause: Stage 4 sits after a single Stage 3; the coordinator created eight Stage-3s and still only one Stage-4. The agent cannot validate itself (P-18), so the only gate is a coordinator round-trip whose latency equals the length of the whole sequential run.
sources: coordinator, B1, B2, B3, B4, B6, B8

verdict.reason:

Dispatch/return times reconstructed from tool_use/tool_result ids: B1 dispatched 18:25:20.709, returned 18:39:52.756. 21:32:41 − 18:39:52.756 = 2h52m48.2s. Claimed "2h52m49s" — exact.
Full sequence (Tehran): full-mode 17:34:32→18:21:16 (46m43s); B1 18:25:20→18:39:52 (14m32s); B2 →18:51:30 (11m04s); B3 →19:17:28 (25m24s); B4 →20:01:17 (43m19s); B5 →20:15:01 (13m06s); B6 →20:54:23 (38m41s); B7 →21:09:12 (14m17s); B8 →21:31:47 (22m09s). All eight strictly sequential, zero overlap.

CONFIRMED — class counts, verbatim from 21:32:51: 1086 "reference row 'X' is missing declared field 'X'", 525 "expr identifier 'X' is not declared…", 355 "row 'X' member 'X' is not a declared field", 34 "processes[] link…", 21 "constant output None carries no value or range". Exact.

CONFIRMED — B4/B6 identity is class-for-class, count-for-count: both 260 expr-identifier / 74 row-member / 8 constant-carries-expr / 7 constant-no-value / 4 processes[] / 4 primaryKey / 1 reference-row = 358. And B6's dispatch prompt (20:15:42) explicitly says "**B4 is the important one.** … **Follow B4's granularity decision exactly** … Mirror B4's key shapes". B4 returned 20:01:17; B6 was dispatched 14m25s later. A validate of B4's part in that window would have made B6's 358 errors impossible.

CONFIRMED — root cause, mechanism 1: the agent genuinely cannot validate itself. data-repo/.claude/agents/quantify.md frontmatter is `tools: Read, Glob, Write` — no Bash. I grepped all nine subagent transcripts for a `validate facts-delta` Bash call: 0 in every one. The only possible gate is a coordinator round-trip. P-18's premise holds.

CONFIRMED — root cause, mechanism 2: skills/quantify/SKILL.md has exactly one Stage 3 ("Task: quantify … Wait for it to complete") followed by exactly one Stage 4 ("Bash: … validate facts-delta {run_dir}/facts-delta.json"). The words "partial", "batch", "per-part" and "chunk" appear nowhere in the playbook (the single "split" hit is Stage C-c grouping findings). The eight-way split was improvised with no playbook gate to reuse — as claimed.

COST OF THE MISSING GATE (measured, not asserted). I re-ran the validator: single part in isolation = 0.54–0.68 s (B1 0.68, B3 0.55, B4 0.54, B6 0.64); the full 499-entry / 975 KB delta took ~2 s in the run itself (21:32:41→21:32:43). Per-part validation is also technically feasible — each part is a self-contained {schema_version, entries} document and B1/B3 validate standalone today. So the claimed "30-second validate" overstates the gate's cost by ~50x; it was a sub-second check.

EXTRA COST NOT IN THE CLAIM: the coordinator's first triage attempt at 21:33:12 was BLOCKED by the data-repo guard hook ("runtime cannot edit .claude/** or CLAUDE.md (INV-2)") because it cd'd into the scratchpad, costing another round-trip before it could split the pile at 21:33:23.

THE ONE WRONG CLAUSE. "A 30-second validate after B1 would have corrected the process-ref convention and the `name`-vs-`key` convention for the remaining seven passes" is not supported. B1's 11 errors were only two classes: 10 × processes[] link + 1 × rule-with-inputs-no-expr. There is no name-vs-key class in B1 at all (the "input/output key 'X' is not a minted segment" class first appears in the SECOND validate round at 22:19, and only in B4/B6). Counting the classes B1 actually exposed across the later parts: processes[] link 24 more (B2 10, B3 3, B4 4, B6 4, B8 3) + rule-no-expr 4 more (B2 1, B8 2, no-key 1) = ~28 of the 2,057 remaining errors, i.e. ~1.4%. The three dominant classes — reference-row-missing-field 1086, expr-identifier 525, row-member 355 = 1,966 (95%) — came from conventions B1 never exercised: B3's reference-record row shape (its own reported "dropped the zero cells" simplification) and B4/B6's rule `expr` declarations. A B1-only gate was nearly worthless; a gate after EVERY part is what the evidence supports.

MINOR IMPRECISION: "eight agents independently repeated the same mistakes with no feedback" — they were not independent. B6's prompt orders "**Read the previous passes first** (…B1.json … B5.json)". They had each other's unvalidated output as input, which propagated the bad conventions rather than merely coinciding on them. This makes the missing gate worse, not better.

VERDICT: problem real, root cause correct, severity high correct.

title: The eight-way split is improvised: no partial mode exists in the agent contract, the playbook or the spec
description: The agent contract documents exactly three modes (manifest, full, targeted) and one output path. All eight dispatches sent `mode: full` and then overrode it in prose with a hand-written preamble inventing a partial pass, a `parts/` directory, per-batch temp-id blocks and a concatenation step. None of the coordination invariants of that scheme — per-part validation, id-block allocation, cross-part refs, key-space partitioning — were designed, reviewed or checked, and the parts directory is invisible to the playbook's own Stage 0 resume logic, so a crash at 20:00 would have discarded four finished parts.
evidence: quantify.md:19 'one of three modes'; :231 'For full and targeted mode: write {run_dir}/facts-delta.json'. grep of the 675-line SKILL.md for batch/split/parts/parallel/sequential finds nothing about splitting a department. Dispatch text: '## IMPORTANT — this is a PARTIAL pass (batch 3 of 8)', 'Temp ids: use only the 3000-block', 'the playbook merges the eight parts itself'. SKILL.md Stage 0: '{run_dir}/facts-delta.json absent → re-enter at Gate A' — that file did not exist between 18:25 and 21:32. Key collisions still leaked: coordinator noted 'pass 8 also touched those keys … pitza__mojudi_akhar_shab'. parts/ also holds an orphan facts-delta-B6-rules-fixed.json matching no B<N> slot.
root_cause: The playbook has one mode (whole department, one delta) and no fallback for an input set that exceeds the output cap, so the coordinator invented an unreviewed protocol mid-run — including the two rules that caused the worst defects (copy the predecessor's conventions; records are per-workbook).
sources: B1, B2, B3, B4, B7, coordinator

verdict.reason:

CONTRACT HAS THREE MODES, ONE OUTPUT PATH — CONFIRMED. .claude/agents/quantify.md:19 "one of three modes, chosen by the dispatch:" followed by a table of exactly manifest | full | targeted. Output contract at e4b2204 line 228 (line 248 in today's file, not :231 as cited — a 3-line citation slip, immaterial): "For **full** and **targeted** mode: write `{run_dir}/facts-delta.json`". Spec line 1364 repeats "modes (`manifest`, `full`, `targeted`)".

NO SPLIT CONCEPT ANYWHERE — CONFIRMED. `git show e4b2204:.claude/agents/quantify.md | grep -iE "partial|batch|split|parts/|concat|chunk"` → zero hits. Same grep on SKILL.md (667 lines at run time, 675 today) → one hit, line 536, unrelated ("split into two groups" of Gate-C findings). Same grep over the 2415-line spec → no notion of splitting a department across passes. No output-cap fallback either: grep for limit|too large|oversize|budget|64k in both prompts returns only unrelated hits (crash notes about `merge facts` internals).

DISPATCHES — CONFIRMED VERBATIM. 8 Agent dispatches at 18:25:20, 18:40:26, 18:52:03, 19:17:58, 20:01:55, 20:15:42, 20:54:55, 21:09:37, each beginning `mode: full` then "## IMPORTANT — this is a PARTIAL pass (batch N of 8)" / "The department's input set is too large for one delta, so it is split into eight sequential passes." (dispatch_full.txt:50-52). Output redirected in prose: "**Write your delta to `.../parts/facts-delta-B1.json`** (NOT to `facts-delta.json` — the playbook merges the eight parts itself)" (:56-58). Per-batch temp-id blocks at dispatch_full.txt:61,105,164,230,305,385,468,551 ("use only the 1000-block … a collision would corrupt the merge"). `grep -ci "mode: partial"` = 0 in both dispatch text and digest; 9 × `mode: full` (8 partials + the original crashed full pass).

Digest line 180: the top-level facts-delta.json was first written at 21:32:36 — i.e. absent for the whole 3h07m of partial passes.

NO PER-PART VALIDATION — CONFIRMED AND WORSE THAN STATED. First `validate facts-delta` call is 21:32:41, on the concatenated 499-entry delta; 2069 output lines, rc=2. Per-part split of the errors: B1 11, B2 21, B3 1306, B4 358, B5 0, B6 358, B7 0, B8 12. No part was ever validated alone. The agent contract never asks the agent to validate; validation is Stage 4, defined only over the single `{run_dir}/facts-delta.json` — so per-part validation had no home in the design.

KEY COLLISION LEAK — CONFIRMED. Digest 21:33:26 "--- non-T-prefixed --- pitza__mojudi_akhar_shab … / mojudi_avval_shab__from_akhar_shab_prev …" and the B1 fix message (digest:194) "pass 8 also touched those keys".

ROOT-CAUSE RULES — CONFIRMED VERBATIM. dispatch_full.txt:113 "**Records are per-workbook** (`{short}__{tab}` …), so each ناهارخوران tab does get its own record"; :114 "keep B1's ASCII tab-name conventions exactly"; :117 "Keep B1's other conventions"; repeated as "Conventions to keep:" at :244, :317, :412, :498. The claim does not attribute it to the split, but a redesign should not chase it here.
verdict.corrected:

(3) Citation `quantify.md:231` should be :228 in the run-time version (e4b2204) / :248 in today's file; SKILL.md was 667 lines at run time, 675 today.

title: The batch axis cut across the reference graph, so cross-entry links were unwritable and are now permanently missing
description: Temp ids are file-local, so an entry in one part cannot reference an entry minted in another; splitting items into B1 and their records into B2 made the item→record `of` edge impossible to write, and `merge facts apply` cannot recover it afterwards. The same fracture broke the mirror graph: B5/B7 minted the mirror records after B4/B6 had already written the rules that should point at them, so 70 mirrors have zero inbound rule edges and 71 rule members name a bare `Table_*` string instead. Where cross-part refs did work, they worked by luck — B4 emitted 12 refs to B1 lines it never read and B7 emitted 12 refs to a part it never opened.
evidence: B2 summary: «پیوند `of` … نوشته نشد، چون اقلام در دلتای پاس اول با شناسه موقت زندگی می‌کنند». Store: F-00146 (B1) has 10 of 13 fields with `of`; F-00159 (B2) has 0 of 13. records.json: 70 role:mirror, 0 in-edges from non-mirrors; 188 rule io members carry no {ref} at all, 35 distinct Table_* names appear as strings in 65 places. B4 referenced T-1036…T-1050, all beyond line 1514 of B1, having read only lines 1–1339 and 1355–1514.
root_cause: The split was made by workbook and by artefact type, i.e. along the axes the estate happens to have, while the schema's links run item→record, rule→record and rule→mirror. No id manifest or key registry was published between passes.
sources: B2, B4, B7, rules audit, records audit, duplication audit

verdict.reason:
The symptoms are real; the mechanism and root cause are wrong.

WHAT IS CONFIRMED
- records.json: 70 entries with data.role=="mirror". Graph scan over every {ref} in all five store files: 2 mirrors have an in-edge, both from other mirrors; in-edges from non-mirrors = 0. Confirmed.
- rules.json: 477 io members (inputs+outputs); 181 carry from.ref, 187 carry no {ref} object anywhere (claim said 188 — off by one). 35 distinct Table_* names appear as a bare `sheet` string in exactly 65 io members. Confirmed.
- F-00146 (pitza__mojudi_avval_shab, B1): 10 of 13 fields carry `of`. F-00159 (amar_pitza__mojudi_avval_shab, B2): 0 of 13. Confirmed. B2's summary quote is verbatim in its transcript (scratchpad/b2.txt:163).
- B4 read facts-delta-B1.json at offsets 1-30, 30-360, 360-700, 700-1040, 1040-1340, 1355-1515 only (b4.digest.txt lines 109-119), and emitted refs to T-1036…T-1050 (12 ids), which start at line 1556 of that file. Confirmed.
- B7 never opened facts-delta-B3.json (its only delta Reads are B5, B6, B2) yet emitted 34 ref occurrences to 12 B3 ids. Confirmed.

WHAT IS REFUTED
1. "Temp ids are file-local, so an entry in one part cannot reference an entry minted in another" — false. Each pass got its own temp-id block (B1=T-1001.., B2=T-2001.., … B8=T-8001..) and the eight parts were concatenated into ONE facts-delta.json before a single `merge facts apply` (coordinator digest lines 194-204, 490, 510). merge_facts/apply.py builds `by_temp` from the whole delta's entries (`_plan`/`_rewrite_refs`, apply.py:362,522,550), so cross-part T- refs resolve by construction. They demonstrably did: 320 cross-part ref occurrences were written by 6 of the 8 parts (B3→B1 85, B4→B1 44, B5→B1/B3/B4 55, B6→B1 5, B7→B2/B3/B6 55, B8→B1/B3/B4 76). The store now has 1562 F- refs, 0 residual "T-" strings and 0 dangling refs.
2. "No id manifest or key registry was published between passes" — false. From batch 3 onward every dispatch carried the sentence "The eight parts are concatenated into ONE delta … so earlier parts' temp ids are stable and **you may `ref` them directly**", plus a per-part inventory (entry counts, what each part covered, the key conventions) and "Read the previous passes first" with paths (scratchpad/dispatch_full.txt:156-170, 233, 308, 388, 471, 554). The one dispatch that omits that sentence is B2's (dispatch_full.txt:96-125) — and B2 is precisely the pass that reported the `of` link as impossible. So the `of` gap is a prompt-coverage bug in one dispatch, not an architectural impossibility.
3. "splitting items into B1 and their records into B2 made the item→record `of` edge impossible" — the described split never happened. B1 held 52 items AND 13 records and its records carry `of` (10/13 on F-00146). B2 was the ناهارخوران workbooks — records only, items deliberately reused from B1. The axis was workbook/branch, not item-vs-record.
4. "B5/B7 minted the mirrors after B4/B6 wrote the rules that should point at them" as an accident of the axis — B4's dispatch anticipated it and sanctioned the outcome: "Where a formula reads a `Table_*` tab that batch 5 will define, `ref` a stub or leave the cross-record link to the natural key — do not mint the `Table_*` records yourself" (dispatch_full.txt:269-270). B4 chose the natural key. The 65 bare Table_* strings are the coordinator's own option 2, not a link that could not be written.
5. "the mirror graph is fractured" — it is connected in the direction the design requires. All 70 mirrors carry a resolved `mirror_of` back-ref to their source record, 0 dangling (spec §QF-19/QF-9 line 1434, 1444: a one-formula import tab gets `role: mirror`, `mirror_of` and no fields[]). B5/B7 wrote those edges across parts, which is the cross-part link the claim says was impossible.
6. "worked by luck" — both cases landed correct. B4's 12 unread ids: T-1045→item_21, T-1046→item_19, T-1047→item_17, T-1048→item_18, T-1049→item_20, T-1050→item_24 match its own سوخاری row keys one-for-one; T-1036→item_358, T-1037→item_374, T-1039→item_368, T-1040→item_754, T-1041→item_757 match its کانتر row `codes` ##358/##374/##368/##754/##757 one-for-one. title: Nothing anywhere says what a `statement` is for, so provenance leaked into the prose field
description: The delta schema types `statement` as a bare string with no description or constraint; the agent prompt mentions it on four lines, only to say it must be Persian; the playbook gives no style guidance at all; and `merge_facts/ladder.py` classes it a PROSE_LEAF that is 'never compared, never disputed', so no gate ever inspects it. The one place the intent is written down — spec §6, 'what the entry means and, where it matters, why' — never reached the prompt. With no positive definition and no prohibition, the agent narrated the artefact it was reading.
evidence: schemas/facts-delta.schema.json: `statement -> {"type": "string"}` and `title -> {"type": "string"}`, no minLength/pattern/description. quantify.md mentions statement on lines 15, 102, 170, 239; the only constraint is :170 «`title`, `statement`, `aliases` … are Persian». SKILL.md: zero style guidance. ladder.py:6 PROSE_LEAVES; apply.py:369 'prose never disputes'. QF-17 then freezes prose fields so a re-run can never improve one — 'a second run's different wording is discarded'.
root_cause: The semantic contract for the field lives only in the design spec's prose; the agent prompt was written as a mechanics contract (envelope keys, id rules, stub shapes) and never carried it across. Locators already have typed homes in `source[]` and `data.location`, so the statement duplicates provenance instead of carrying meaning.

title: Mirror tabs are mandated as full records rather than a reference on the source
description: Obligation 2 requires a `role: mirror` record with `mirror_of` for every one-formula IMPORT_FROM_SHEET tab, plus the rule that performs the pull. The spec's own §7/QF-10 orders this, treating the import graph as the ERP's most valuable inheritance and materialising every hop as an entity. The result is that a copy of a table becomes an entry with the same standing as the table, while the structural half of the same graph (`foreignKeys`) is used zero times.
evidence: quantify.md:87 'a one-formula IMPORT_FROM_SHEET tab gets role: mirror, mirror_of and no fields[]' and 'per IMPORT_FROM_SHEET a mirror_of and the rule that performs the pull'. Spec :908, :915 and Appendix A :2112 ('112 hidden mirror tabs | record role: mirror | clean'). Store: 70 of 156 records are mirrors, 68 with zero inbound references from non-mirrors; `foreignKeys` 0, `reconciled_against` 0. The pull rules were also not written: 35 IMPORT_FROM_SHEET formulas in B5's workbook produced 0 rules.
root_cause: The design chose completeness of the sheet estate over usefulness of the fact store: a mirror carries no independent quantity, but the contract mints an entity for it anyway. A mirror should be an edge on the source record, not a node.
sources: B5, B7, records audit, duplication audit, spec audit, consumer audit

verdict.reason:
CORE CLAIM CONFIRMED, FOUR SUB-CLAIMS WRONG.

CONFIRMED — the mandate exists and the store shows the waste.
- quantify.md:77 "a one-formula `IMPORT_FROM_SHEET` tab gets `role: mirror`, `mirror_of` and no `fields[]`"; :87 "per `IMPORT_FROM_SHEET` a `mirror_of` and the rule that performs the pull — never a `foreignKeys` member". (The claim cites :87 for the first quote; it is at :77.)
- Spec 2026-08-29-quantitative-facts-design.md:908-909 (§7) and QF-10 at :912 ("that dependency graph *is* the data flow and is the single most useful thing the ERP builder inherits"); Appendix A:2147 "| 112 hidden mirror tabs | `record role: mirror` | clean |".
- facts/records.json: 156 records, role counts {mirror 70, log 58, reference 18, report 8, config 1, checklist 1}. 70/156 = 45% mirrors, 35 per branch (Gozaresh markazi + Gozaresh naharkhoran), 31.6% of records.json bytes (115,230 of 364,291).
- Inbound refs: ALL 70 mirrors have zero inbound references from non-mirror entries; 68 have zero inbound from anything at all (the 2 exceptions are referenced only by other mirrors). The source→mirror→report chain QF-10 was built for was never closed: the 8 `role: report` records cite no mirror.
- Cost in the run: batches B5 (Gozaresh markazi Table_* tabs) and B7 (Gozaresh naharkhoran Table_* tabs) were 2 of the 8 sequential passes, ~13 min and ~15 min wall (digest 20:01:55→20:15:01, 20:54:55→21:09:37), and each produced 50 entries that were 100% `record` — B5's own summary: "۰ قلم، ۰ اندازه‌گیری، ۰ قاعده، ۰ یادداشت". 100 of the 499 delta entries (20%) carried no item, measurement, rule or note.
- Metric corruption (new evidence, not in the claim): all 70 mirrors are `status: confirmed`; every one of the other 86 records is `unknown` (56) or `inferred` (30). The mirrors are the only "confirmed" records in the store, so they inflate QF-44's readiness/red-rollup with entries nobody confirmed.
- Design self-contradiction (new evidence): B6's own report says 28 rules stayed at `lang: "sheets"` and it refused the aggregate form for the four «مصرف واقعی» rules because they "look a code up in a `Table_*` mirror row that batch 7 defines" and "the records in question are the `Table_SalesData_*` / `Table_Ingredients_*` mirrors ... their temp ids and field keys are not knowable here". QF-9 gives a mirror no `fields[]`, so the node the contract mints cannot serve as the `inputs[].from {ref, field}` target that rules need. It mints the entity and denies it the one attribute that would make it referenceable.

REFUTED SUB-CLAIM 1 — "mandated as full records". False. Both the spec (:908, :1163 "mirrors carry no rows") and the prompt explicitly forbid `fields[]`, and the store obeys: 0 of 70 mirrors carry `fields`, 0 carry `rows`. A mirror is already a stub (id, key, title, ~309-char Persian statement, scope, source, `data: {medium, role, location, grain, mirror_of, import, named_range}`). No table content is duplicated. The cost is the entry envelope and the prose, not a copy of the table.

REFUTED SUB-CLAIM 2 — "68 with zero inbound references from non-mirrors". Understated. It is 70/70 from non-mirrors; 68 have zero from anything.

REFUTED SUB-CLAIM 3 — "`foreignKeys` 0 [times used]". Misleading and backwards. The agents wrote 72 `foreignKeys` members in this run: 35 in facts-delta-B5.json, 35 in B7, 1 in B4, 1 in B6 — every mirror got one, in direct violation of the prompt's own "never a `foreignKeys` member". All were malformed: `{spreadsheetId, sheet, range, target}` instead of §8's `{fields, reference, reference_fields}`. `validate facts-delta` passed them silently (B5: 0 errors, B7: 0 errors — the two cleanest passes of the eight), and content.py:371-376 documents why: "84 stored records carried an IMPORT descriptor here instead ... an absent `fields` was an empty list and every one of them passed this pass cleanly." The zero in the store is engine/merge_facts/verbs.py:224 `repair_foreign_keys` retroactively stripping all 84 store-wide. So the structural half was not ignored — it was misused 84 times, passed by the validator, and deleted afterwards.

REFUTED SUB-CLAIM 4 — "The pull rules were also not written: 35 IMPORT_FROM_SHEET formulas in B5's workbook produced 0 rules". False as stated. One pull rule per workbook exists: F-00321 `gozaresh_markazi__fn__import_from_sheet` and F-00394 `gozaresh_naharkhoran__fn__import_from_sheet`, written by B4 and B6, whose statements read "هر ۳۵ تب Table_* این کاربرگ تنها همین یک فرمول را در سلول A1 دارند". B5/B7 wrote 0 rules because their prompts scoped them to `Table_*` tabs only ("this one covers ONE workbook and, inside it, only its `Table_*` tabs"). The agent generalised 35 identical formulas into one shared rule — which is the behaviour the user asks for elsewhere (one shared rule, not one per line), so this is the opposite of a defect.

PARTLY REFUTED — "a mirror carries no independent quantity". Every mirror carries `import` (source file/sheet/range) AND its own `named_range.refers_to`, and comparing the two is what produced the pass's one genuinely valuable output: 38 of 70 mirrors carry `issues[]`, 19 of kind `column_shift`, e.g. F-00203 "محدوده نام‌دار Table_Pizza_Last فقط تا ستون M تعریف شده ... در حالی که خود تب تا ستون O داده دارد" — two ingredient columns (`##33`, `##26`) never reach the report formulas. That defect is a property of the mirror tab, not of the source record, so it needs somewhere to hang; the shared per-workbook pull rule cannot hold 35 different ranges.

ROOT CAUSE — partly right. "Completeness of the sheet estate over usefulness" is correct and Appendix A's census table is the mechanism. But the sharper cause is the QF-9/QF-10 contradiction: QF-10 declares the import graph the most valuable inheritance, then QF-9 strips the mirror of `fields[]`, leaving a node whose entire payload (`import`, `named_range`) is exactly edge data, that no rule can bind to, and that nothing references.

SEVERITY — high is too strong; medium is right. It cost ~28 min of ~3h (15%), 20% of the delta entries, 45% of the final records, and it corrupts the confirmed-count. But B5/B7 were the two zero-error passes, contributed nothing to the 2068-error failure or the output-token crashes, and did yield the 19 column_shift findings — the pass's highest-value output.

The result: 70 of 156 records (45%) are mirrors, 31.6% of records.json bytes; ALL 70 have zero inbound references from non-mirror entries and 68 have zero inbound from anything, so the source→mirror→report chain QF-10 exists for was never closed. Two of the eight sequential passes (B5, B7, ~28 min) were spent on them and produced 100 delta entries containing zero items, measurements, rules or notes. All 70 are `status: confirmed` while every other record is `unknown`/`inferred`, so they are the only confirmed records in the store and inflate QF-44's readiness measure. The design also contradicts itself: QF-9 denies a mirror `fields[]`, so B6 could not bind four «مصرف واقعی» rules to the `Table_*` mirrors and left 28 rules untranslated at `lang: "sheets"` — the contract mints an entity and withholds the attribute that would make it referenceable. (b) `foreignKeys` was not "used zero times" — the agents wrote 72 members in this run (35 in B5, 35 in B7, 1 each in B4/B6), all malformed as `{spreadsheetId, sheet, range, target}` and in violation of the prompt's own "never a `foreignKeys` member"; `validate` passed them silently (content.py:371-376 documents the hole) and `merge facts repair-foreign-keys` (verbs.py:224) later stripped all 84 store-wide. That is a separate, arguably worse finding: a contract field the agent misuses, the validator misses, and a repair verb deletes. (c) the pull rules WERE written — F-00321 and F-00394, one shared rule per workbook covering all 35 tabs each, produced by B4/B6; B5/B7 wrote none because their prompts scoped them to `Table_*` tabs only. Generalising 35 identical formulas into one rule is the behaviour the user wants, not a defect. (d) mirrors are not information-free: `named_range.refers_to` vs the `import` range yielded 19 `column_shift` issues (38 of 70 mirrors carry `issues[]`), including F-00203 where the named range stops at column M while the tab has data to O, so two ingredient columns never reach the report formulas — the mirror pass's highest-value output. Severity: medium, not high — B5/B7 were the only two passes with zero validation errors and contributed nothing to the 2068-error failure or the output-token crashes.

title: Process anchoring (obligation 8) is unbounded work with no index, and degraded silently to title-only skims
description: The prompt requires that an entry citing a process quote a node whose label or description names the entry's referent, and the dispatch hands over the department's whole process corpus as raw JSON globs. Cooking has 36 process files totalling ~1.9 MB against a 25K-token Read cap, so every pass self-rationed: reading titles only, or copying whichever two processes the previous pass had used. Agents then reported negative findings ('no node names these tabs') they had no evidence for.
evidence: departments/cooking/processes/ = 36 files, 1,806,107 B. Full-mode run: 34 of 36 read with `limit: 4` (87-151 char results = id/department/name only). B1 read 4 in full then issued `limit: 5` on the other 32 and still concluded «هیچ گرهی آن‌ها را نام نمی‌برد». B2 read only cooking-030 (truncated at 1150/1814) and cooking-032 — exactly the two B1 had used — and attached a cooking-030-n016 quote to 9 of 18 entries. B3 opened 12 of 36, eight of them at `limit: 4`. B5/B7 never opened any, yet asserted no process anchor exists. Store-wide: 34 of 486 entries carry a processes[] link, naming 3 of 36 files.
root_cause: An obligation whose cost scales with the department's whole process corpus, with no budget, no index of node labels, no Grep in the toolset and no per-entry lookup mechanism. Nothing requires the summary to distinguish 'checked and absent' from 'not checked'.
sources: full-mode transcript audit, B1, B2, B3, B5, B7, consumer audit

title: The prompt lists only required keys, so the optional-but-load-bearing payload fields are invisible and were never used
description: The agent prompt carries a required-keys table per kind and defers the payload vocabulary to a 1,500-line spec. Every optional field that carries the value an ERP actually needs is therefore unused, while the agent invented 15+ ad-hoc keys to hold information the contract had no home for. Seven of eleven `item` fields, the three ERP-critical edges, and the whole uncertainty machinery on records are dead.
evidence: Across 139 items the only data keys are {category, unit, code, unit_ref}: `group`, `state`, `grade`, `units[]`, `pack`, `tracked`, `code_absent` are used 0 times — so a 330 ml can and a 1.5 l family bottle are both `unit: pcs`. `foreignKeys` 0, `reconciled_against` 0, `template_of` 0, `header_fields` 0, `refItems` 0, `cadence` 0, `movement` 0, `place` items 0. `fields[].description` 0 of 496. Invented instead: `unit_ref` ×137, `bindings` ×41 (318 per-cell entries), `import`/`named_range` ×70 each, `applies_to` ×19, `row_meta` ×10, `frequency` ×11, `column` on 488 of 496 fields. F-00304 is the spec's own worked example for `item.units[]`, written as a measurement instead.
root_cause: Optional fields have no prompt-level presence and no schema enforcement, so they are invisible unless the agent re-reads the spec; and `data` is `additionalProperties: true`, so an invented key is cheaper than finding the right one.
sources: items/measurements audit, records audit, consumer audit, rules audit

title: The prompt calls the JSON schema authoritative, but the real contract is 32 undocumented rules in engine/merge_facts/content.py
description: The schema types every `data` payload as an open object with a required-key list and no enums, so it cannot express any of the rules that actually decide pass/fail. Those live only in Python, and at least 18 of the 32 check families are never stated in the agent prompt — including the single fact (inputs/outputs members are keyed by `key`, not `name`) that produced 525 of the 2,068 errors. The coordinator's own fix messages repeated the false claim that the schema is authoritative, and one agent had to reverse-engineer the contract from the engine's test file.
evidence: schemas/facts-delta.schema.json: rule branch requires only `[inputs, outputs]`; `data: {"type": "object"}`. quantify.md output contract: 'the file is authoritative on the exact shape'. Never stated in the prompt: members keyed by `key`; rows restricted to RESERVED_ROW_NAMES + declared field keys; primaryKey/foreignKeys membership; reference-row completeness; constant-vs-rule shape; the FEEL keyword whitelist (content.py:38, 12 tokens); the `sum over … of` aggregate form; that a processes[] link needs a process-type source whose `ref` ends `{id}.json`. B6 at 21:36:50: 'Every expr identifier was rejected, even plainly-declared ones. I need the validator's actual rule'; at 21:39:07 it found it in engine/tests/test_validate_facts_content.py. Both of B7's and B8's Writes pass jsonschema with 0 errors while failing the content pass.
root_cause: Task 1 froze the schema as shape-and-enum only and Task 9 put every cross-field rule in Python, but the prompt was written pointing at the schema rather than at a transcription of the content pass. No task owns 'the agent knows every rule the validator enforces'.
sources: B1, B2, B3, B4, B6, B8, plan-vs-implementation, coordinator

verdict.reason:
P-17 CONFIRMED in substance; two sub-claims are wrong and need correcting.

VERIFIED
1. Schema is shape-only. schemas/facts-delta.schema.json (116 lines): envelope `data: {"type":"object"}`; the five kind branches add ONLY required-key lists — item [category,unit], record [medium,role,location], measurement [quantity,unit], rule [inputs,outputs], note []. No enum, no member shape, no cross-field rule anywhere inside `data`. Nothing in it can express any of the 12 content-pass families.
2. content.py = exactly 32 `messages.append` sites (`grep -c` → 32) across 12 numbered check families. The claim's "32 rules" is right; "32 check families" is the wrong unit (12 families, 32 messages).
3. Measured schema-vs-content gap, running Draft202012Validator + merge_facts.content.check_document over the eight pre-fix part writes captured in scratchpad: EVERY part = 0 jsonschema errors. Content errors: b1 11, b2 21, B3 1306, b4 372, b6 372, B5 70, b7 70, b8 14. Sum 2236 vs the run's 2068 — same picture. The claim's "B7's and B8's Writes pass jsonschema with 0 errors while failing the content pass" is true and is true of all eight.
4. Prompt points at the schema, states almost none of the rules. agents/quantify.md: "`schema_path` … The enforced contract for the file you are about to write; the tables below summarise it, the file is authoritative"; output contract: "the file is authoritative on the exact shape". Grep for inputs/outputs/RESERVED/primaryKey/foreignKeys/expr/FEEL/"sum over"/share over quantify.md returns 7 hits, none of which state a content rule. All 8 dispatch prompts (scratchpad/bprompts.txt) say only "validated against `facts-delta.schema.json`" — no content rules either.
5. Of the 32 messages I count ~23 with NO counterpart in quantify.md. Stated: unit-edge `via` (obl. 7), processes[] id grammar, foreignKeys "every member carries both of its sides" (2 messages), the .structure.md/NAMED_FUNCTIONS.md exclusion. Partial: minted-segment grammar (given for entry `key`s, never said to apply to fields/inputs/outputs members — nor that those members have a `key` at all), field_status values, Jalali dates, and processes[]-needs-a-process-source (stated in two separate halves — obl. 8 "cite that node as a `process` source" + the ref-path rule "a process → departments/{dept}/processes/{pid}.json" — never as one rule; 34 errors of this type still occurred). So "at least 18 of 32" holds and is conservative.
6. B6's quotes are verbatim and correctly attributed. subagents/agent-a6bcbaa3c3e516146.jsonl (meta: "Quantify batch 6 naharkhoran report rules"): 21:36:50 "Every `expr` identifier was rejected, even plainly-declared ones. I need the validator's actual rule — let me find it."; 21:37:05 Read engine/tests/test_validate_facts_content.py; 21:39:07 "Found it. The tests reveal the actual contract: `inputs[]`/`outputs[]` members are keyed by **`key`**, not `name` … and the identifier check only runs for `lang: "feel"`."
7. Root cause CONFIRMED from the plan. docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-30-quantitative-facts.md Task 9 enumerates all 12 checks including the keyword set verbatim `{if,then,else,and,or,not,min,max,sum,abs,round,over,of}`. Task 14 Step 1 defines the agent body as "the QF-19 obligations transcribed in full from the spec" + non-negotiables + "the delta contract: output … conforming to `facts-delta.schema.json`" — the content pass is not mentioned. Task 14 Step 3's verification is "validate the example delta … against `facts-delta.schema.json`". No task owns "the agent knows every rule the validator enforces". Confirmed.

CONTRARY EVIDENCE (three corrections)
A. "Those live only in Python" is FALSE. The rules are written out in prose in the design spec: §7 line 1026-1037 gives the FEEL subset including "identifiers from `inputs[].key` and `outputs[].key`" and the aggregate form; §12 line 1309-1320 lists the whole content pass (reserved row member names, membership, reference-row completeness, share sums, constant-rule shape, field_status, reconciled_against). They also live in plan Task 9. The failure is not that they were never written down — it is that no document the agent is handed contains them: quantify.md transcribes §13's nine obligations but not §7's payload grammar or §12's content list.
B. The 525-error attribution is FALSE. Counterfactual replay on B4's own pre-fix write (scratchpad/b4_write2.json): renaming every inputs/outputs `name`→`key` moves expr-identifier errors 260 → 225 (only ~13% fixed) and RAISES total errors 372 → 430, because the agent's names are camelCase/non-segment and now trip "input/output key is not a minted segment". The live run confirms it — after B6 applied exactly that rename, 22:19:05 still shows 247 expr-identifier + 91 "input key not a minted segment" + 28 "output key not a minted segment", and 22:21:13 still 225 expr-identifier. The residual identifiers are invented function calls (getRowByPersianDate 13, getIngredientValueById 12, format 3, format_persian_date 2, index_of, matches, column, date_value), the loop tokens `for` 4 / `in` 4, and never-declared names (ruz 17, mah 17, sal 17, mojudi_avval_shab 4). B6's own "that's why all 260 identifiers failed" was itself a wrong diagnosis, and P-17 repeats it.
C. "The FEEL keyword whitelist (content.py:38, 12 tokens)" — it is 13 tokens at content.py:38-39 (len(KEYWORDS)==13).
D. Minor: the coordinator repeated "the schema is authoritative" in 4 of 6 fix messages (2026-09-02T18:04:10Z B1 "the schema file is authoritative — re-read it", 18:04:25Z B2, 18:04:46Z B3 "it is the authoritative contract", 18:05:48Z B8). The B4 (18:05:09Z) and B6 (18:05:27Z) messages actually said "Re-read `facts-delta.schema.json` first — the content pass enforces more than the JSON shape", i.e. partially corrected. "Repeated" is right for the majority, not for all.

BONUS FINDING supporting the problem: `_check_key_list` (content.py:270) only fires when `key` is PRESENT and malformed, so a member with `name` and no `key` — the exact B4/B6 shape — produces no message about the missing key at all; it surfaces only as downstream "expr identifier is not declared" noise. The validator cannot say the one thing the agent needed to hear.

SEVERITY: high is correct. 100% of the run's 2068 validation failures were content-pass failures and 0 were schema failures, against a prompt that names the schema as the contract.
verdict.corrected:
The prompt calls the JSON schema authoritative, but the real pass/fail contract is 32 checks (12 families) in engine/merge_facts/content.py that the schema cannot express and the prompt never states.

The schema types every `data` payload as an open object with a required-key list and no enums (rule branch requires only [inputs, outputs]; `data: {"type": "object"}`), so it carries none of the rules that actually decide pass/fail. Those rules ARE written down — in the design spec §7 (the FEEL subset, the reserved row names) and §12 (the whole content-pass list), and in plan Task 9 — but in no document the agent is handed: quantify.md transcribes §13's nine QF-19 obligations and points at the schema, and all 8 dispatch prompts say only "validated against facts-delta.schema.json". Roughly 23 of the 32 messages have no counterpart in the prompt; 5 are stated and ~4 only in halves.

The cost is measurable: all eight pre-fix part writes pass jsonschema with 0 errors while producing 11–1306 content errors each (B3 alone 1306 with 0 schema errors); all 2068 run failures were content-pass failures and none were schema failures. The 525 "expr identifier is not declared" errors were produced by the undocumented FEEL contract as a whole — the 13-token keyword whitelist (content.py:38-39), "every identifier must be declared", members keyed by `key` not `name`, and keys that must be minted segments — not by any single fact: replaying the `name`→`key` rename on B4's own write fixes only 260→225 of its identifier errors and adds 119 new "key is not a minted segment" errors, exactly as the live run shows after B6 applied it (247 identifier errors still at 22:19:05, 225 at 22:21:13). Root cause as stated is correct: Task 1 froze the schema as shape-and-required-keys only, Task 9 put every cross-field rule in Python (and in its own plan text), and Task 14 wrote the prompt pointing at the schema, verifying it only against the schema. No task owns "the agent knows every rule the validator enforces". A related defect: content.py never reports a member that has no `key` at all, so the one diagnosis the agent needed is unreportable.

title: The agent cannot run the validator it is graded by — no Bash means no self-check at any point
description: The toolset is Read/Glob/Write, so the agent cannot run `validate facts-delta`, cannot count its own entries, cannot measure its own file size and cannot check a fix. Every structural error therefore survives to the coordinator, and the error latency equals the length of the whole sequential run. One agent said so explicitly in its own report.
evidence: quantify.md:5 `tools: Read, Glob, Write`. B4's closing line: 'I could not re-run `validate` myself (no shell in this session), so these fixes are reasoned from the error list, not verified.' B1's fix round replaced 11 errors with 6 new ones and reported 'Nothing left unfixed'; a third round three hours later finally passed. B2's own fix `item_20 != null` was itself invalid because `null` is not in content.py's 12-token keyword set. The validator is a 2-second deterministic CLI.
root_cause: The tool allowlist was written to enforce INV-1 (the agent never writes facts/**) and removed execution wholesale rather than allowlisting a read-only validate command. The guard should restrict what can be executed, not whether anything can be.
sources: B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B7, B8, full-mode transcript audit

verdict.reason:
Every offered evidence item checks out, and two extra checks make the problem stronger than stated.

TOOLSET. data-repo/.claude/agents/quantify.md:5 = `tools: Read, Glob, Write` — confirmed. It is not an accident of an over-broad allowlist: the spec states it deliberately at code-repo/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-29-quantitative-facts-design.md:1434 (QF-19) — "`model: claude-opus-5[1m]`, `tools: Read, Glob, Write` — no Bash, no ids, no hashing". It is also uniform house style: none of the five data-repo agents has Bash (extract `Read, Write`; classify `Read, Grep, Glob, Write`; summarize/consolidate `Read, Glob, Write`).

THE AGENT SAID SO. agent-a8fea49a9665e4d96.jsonl (= B4, "Quantify batch 4 central report rules") contains verbatim: "could not re-run `validate` myself (no shell in this session), so these fixes are reasoned from the error list, not verified."

THE AGENT COULD NOT HAVE REASONED IT OUT EITHER. engine/validate/cli.py runs jsonschema FIRST and exits 2 before the content pass; the run reached the content pass, so the delta was schema-clean and all 2068 errors came from engine/merge_facts/content.py. The dispatch prompts told each batch its delta must be "validated against `facts-delta.schema.json`" — an artifact in which none of the failing rules exist. The only readable source of those rules is content.py, which no prompt names.

title: A wrong line in the prompt put 84 malformed foreignKeys into the store, past both the schema and the validator
description: Obligation 2 as live during the run told the agent to write a `foreignKeys` row for every IMPORT_FROM_SHEET mirror, contradicting the spec (a mirror has no fields[] to join on) and the prompt's own later text. The schema has no foreignKeys definition at all, and the content pass read `fk.get("fields") or []` so an absent required key validated vacuously. 84 members reached the store across nine departments' runs, crashed the UI, and needed a purpose-built engine verb to remove because the write ladder has no removal action.

B5's own summary claims it as an achievement: «۳۵ رکورد آینه … هرکدام با mirror_of و یک ردیف foreignKeys». content.py:372 docstring: '84 stored records carried an IMPORT descriptor here instead … and every one of them passed this pass cleanly.' UI crash at RecordCard.tsx:662 `fk.fields.join`. Fixed 2026-09-06: prompt bc53b2d, validator 5862498, repair verb 4a513f5 ('a verb that removes, because the ladder never can').

title: USER COMPLAINT — statements cite sheet cells, tabs and filenames, defeating the purpose of the store
description: The facts store exists so nobody has to open the spreadsheets, and 95% of its statements are spreadsheet navigation instructions. Locators are already carried structurally in `source[]`, `data.location` and `data.bindings`, so the prose duplicates machine fields instead of stating what the fact means. The one place the intent is written down is the spec's §6 exemplar, «مصرف اعلامی = موجودی اول شب + دریافت از انبار − موجودی آخر شب», which contains no locator at all.
evidence: 468 of 486 statements contain تب|برگه|فایل|ستون|سلول|ردیف|محدوده; 257 (53%) OPEN with a locator word, including 155 of 156 records and 100 of 156 rules; 196 carry a bare A1 cell reference; 291 name an .xlsx; 133 name a Table_* mirror tab. Examples: F-00337 «سلول B4 تب پیتزا روز تاریخ گزارش را مستقیم از سلول C5 تب «تاریخ» می‌خواند.»; F-00355 «ستون H تب فرنگی (گروه H6:H14): موجودی اول شب به‌علاوه دریافت از انبار منهای موجودی آخر شب.»; F-00202 «تب پنهان «Table_Pizza_First» … تنها یک فرمول در A1 دارد که با IMPORT_FROM_SHEET محدوده A:S … را می‌آورد.» Only 2 rule statements in the whole store read as business facts without the sheet.
root_cause: P-13 (statement is unspecified) plus P-11 (the walk is tab-by-tab, so the tab is the most salient noun in context when the sentence is written). The per-batch dispatches also repeated 'cite the workbook cell' without distinguishing source[] citation from prose.
sources: user, prose audit, B1, B2, B3, B4, B5, B6, B7, records audit, rules audit

title: USER COMPLAINT — one rule per line and per branch instead of one shared rule
description: The same computation is written once per production line and once per branch, so 14 rule families of 8 members each account for 100 of the 156 rules. Across the 75 rules that carry an expression there are only 30 distinct strings, and the same expression is even spelled two different ways depending on which pass wrote it. An ERP builder facing eight copies of the deviation rule cannot tell which is authoritative — the exact failure the spec's QF-16 warns about.
evidence: Normalising branch and line out of rule keys gives 14 families covering 100 of 156 rules: `__ruz`, `__mah`, `__sal`, `__mojudi_avval_shab`, `__daryaft_az_anbar`, `__mojudi_akhar_shab`, `__masraf_elami`, `__masraf_vaqei`, `__enheraf`, `__flag_enheraf_mosbat`, `__flag_enheraf_manfi` (×8 each) plus three ×4. `masraf_vaqei - masraf_elami` appears as F-00345/357/369/378 (chalebagh) and F-00418/430/442/451 (naharkhoran). F-00355 and F-00428 have byte-identical statements. 154 of 156 rules are scoped to one branch; 146 of 156 keys are prefixed gozaresh_markazi__/gozaresh_naharkhoran__, though the two workbooks share 78 of their 86/79 distinct formula shapes (Jaccard 0.90). 12 exact-duplicate title pairs exist.

On the LINE axis it is not literal copying: only 16 of 28 line families share a single formula; the other 12 have genuinely different text per line because each line reads a different Table_* tab and a different item id (e.g. mojudi_avval_shab: Table_Pizza_First/id 1 vs Table_Farangi_First/id 14 vs Table_Fried_First/id 21 vs Table_KitchenCounter_First/SUM over ids 101,102,...). Those are parameterisations of one rule, not duplicates — the right shape is one rule with a per-line parameter table, and a naive dedupe would lose the bindings. So: the branch fanout should be deleted outright; the line fanout should be collapsed into one rule plus a parameter table.

(2) "The exact failure QF-16 warns about" overstates the mechanism — QF-16 is about display-name aliasing creating duplicates, not line/branch fanout. But its stated harm is realised here, and there is a concrete instance the evidence list misses: F-00320 and F-00393 (the two copies of the CONVERT_GR_TO_KG rule) contradict each other about which columns carry the 1000x scale error, while the dumps show both workbooks call that function in the identical column set. One is wrong, both are open, neither carries accounts[], and nothing marks which is authoritative.

Also add to the root cause: the fanout is positively mandated, not merely unprevented (quantify.md obligation 2, "per formula group one rule keyed by output", with QF-32's per-workbook-per-tab key grammar; the spec's only dedup rule, QF-31, dedups only within a formula group). And a third cause the claim omits — the engine cannot see the duplication: apply.py `_title_twin` refuses byte-equal titles only within the same canonical scope, and audit.py `_lookalike_title` deliberately skips byte-identical values assuming apply caught them, so per-branch scoping lets all 12 byte-identical title pairs through both gates silently.

Finally: "defended it twice against its own fix round" — the order is documented verbatim (bprompts.txt:399,405) and reaffirmed once in the fix round (ffa1_digest.txt:202, "keep the two branches structurally in step"); a second explicit defense is not in the transcript, though the final report does present the branch pairs as normal rather than as a defect.

title: USER COMPLAINT — mirror tables recorded as entries at all

title: USER COMPLAINT — useless notes: things that should be rules, and worthless trivia
description: Of 22 notes, only one is genuinely a note; 18 are entries the spec's own classification ladder routes to a different kind, and 3 are droppable trivia. The note kind is the only one with no required data keys and no schema constraint, so it is strictly cheaper to emit than any other kind — and `merge facts apply` explicitly exempts notes from its duplicate guard. Twenty of the 22 came from a single pass, where `note` was effectively the default kind.
evidence: F-00465: a note whose entire content is that a cell carries the comment «149», and whose own statement says «معنای این کامنت … مشخص نیست» (the estate's whole comment corpus is two rows, both the string '149'). F-00485: carton ventilation holes. F-00475: a next-day meeting time. Misfiled: F-00467/F-00468 (the 'we do not track X' content that `item.tracked` exists for — used 0 of 139 times), F-00470/471/472 (waste routing, a rule with `lang: text` — used 1 of 156 times), F-00478 (a review threshold ≈300, a constant). parts/facts-delta-B8.json: 39 entries = 20 note, 13 measurement, 4 rule, 2 record. schema: `{"kind": "note", "data": {"type": "object"}}`. apply.py:336 `if entry["kind"] != "note":` guards the title-twin check.
root_cause: §8's ladder ends in an unconditional 'None of the above → note' with no negative test, and the note payload is schema-unconstrained. The spec also promises a statement-hash key for notes that the QF-32 key table never defines and `merge` never derives, so notes have neither an idempotence guard nor a duplicate guard.
sources: user, notes audit, B1, B2, B8, records audit

verdict.reason:
