- Schema (code-repo/schemas/facts-delta.schema.json): `{ "properties": { "kind": { "const": "note" }, "data": { "type": "object" } } }` — note is the only one of the five kinds with no required data keys. The agent prompt reproduces this as a table row: quantify.md:269 `| note | (no additional required keys) |`. Cheapest kind to emit, confirmed.
- Duplicate-guard exemption exists, at engine/merge_facts/apply.py:387 (NOT :336): `if entry["kind"] != "note":  # QF-34` guarding `_title_twin`. The spec's named backstop does not compensate: `merge facts audit` on the live store emits 0 `recurring_note_shape` findings (only 62 row_gone, 15 unconsumed_constant, 7 unknown_role, 4 duplicate_output). The real duplicate pair F-00466/F-00473 (both "meaning of the two count columns in tab «OFF اجرایی»") scores token overlap 0.42 against audit.py's NOTE_OVERLAP = 0.7, and their `_shape` differs — so it is missed.

Agent obligation 5 (quantify.md:99) even names "`item.tracked` exceptions" as a transcript deliverable. §8 step 3 routes F-00470/471/472 (waste routing, no formula) to `rule lang: text`; `lang: text` = 1 of 156 rules (F-00461, and even that one has non-empty inputs). §8 step 8 routes F-00478's ≈300 review threshold to a constant rule. §8 step 4 routes F-00474 (خوب/متوسط/بد) to `record.fields[].constraints.enum`. §2 explicitly puts "a tracking policy" in scope.
- My own pass over all 22 against the §8 ladder reproduces the claimed split within judgment noise (~18 routed elsewhere, 3 droppable, ~1 arguably genuine).
- Worse than claimed: exactly 1 of 22 notes carries any numeric value in `data` — F-00485's `vents_per_carton: 3`, i.e. the trivia entry — and 12 of 22 have `data: {"about": …}` and nothing else. The ≈300 threshold, the tracking policy and the waste routing exist only as untyped Persian prose in `statement`. In a quantitative-facts store the note kind yielded one number, from the one entry everyone agrees is junk.

WRONG IN THE EVIDENCE
- "the estate's whole comment corpus is two rows, both the string '149'" is false. attachments/sheets/.dump/*/comments.tsv holds 102 comment rows across 5 workbooks (81 + 10 + 6 + 3 + 2). Only Kanter.xlsx (19jHmcKHJm8aOOef8kuiTRuGrswmUs4TKDaM1aAchwRk) has exactly 2, both "149". This cuts against the claim's wording but makes the underlying problem worse: ~90 of those comments carry real quantities («الف: 2.305 kg از راسته / ب: 0.845 kg از گردن»), and the run's single comment-sourced fact is the worthless one.

ROOT CAUSE — PARTLY WRONG, AND INCOMPLETE
1. "the QF-32 key table never defines [a statement-hash key]" is false. §5's table has the row `| note | note_ + the first 12 hex of sha256(statement) — deterministic |`. What is true is the consequence: `merge` never derives or enforces it — `_derive_keys` (apply.py:110) owns only measurement keys and record row keys by its own docstring ("the two keys `merge` owns") — and the rule appears nowhere in the agent prompt. 0 of 22 stored notes carry a `note_<hash>` key; 0 of 22 satisfy the spec's companion rule `title` = first 60 chars of `statement`. So the idempotence guard is absent in fact, but not for the stated reason.
2. "§8's ladder ends in an unconditional 'None of the above → note' with no negative test" quotes §8 correctly (step 13) but is not the operative cause: §8 is never given to the agent. quantify.md:104 says "Classify with §8 in order" while §8 lives in code-repo's spec, is in none of the agent's declared inputs (only `schema_path` is passed), and its text appears nowhere in quantify.md or skills/quantify/SKILL.md (greps for "Varies by condition", "controlled vocabulary", "escape hatch", "sha256" over both files return nothing but one unrelated hit).

title: USER COMPLAINT — notes and facts duplicated per branch
description: Branch scope is assigned from whichever source happened to mention the fact, not from where the fact holds, so a definition documented once from a sheet and once from a transcript becomes two branch-local entries. The note store is lopsided by source rather than by content: 19 of 22 notes are chalebagh-only because all three transcripts read were chalebagh meetings. The same happens at scale for records and rules.
evidence: F-00466 `ashpazkhne_naharkhoran__off_ejraei__tedad_nafar_kasb_shode` (from B2, sheet source, scope naharkhoran) and F-00473 `off_ejraei__mani_do_sotoon` (from B8, voice source, scope chalebagh) define the same two columns of the same tab; F-00473's data literally carries the field keys `target_count`/`achieved_count` of records F-00143/F-00156. One waste policy is split three ways across F-00470/471/472. Note branch scopes: chalebagh 19, both 2, naharkhoran 1. 131 record/rule clusters differ only by a branch token; 126 of them were produced by two different passes.
root_cause: QF-43 attributes scope from the source artefact, which is the wrong axis for a branch-independent definition; the natural key includes branches, so two branch copies can never merge; and the eight passes were split so that no pass ever saw both copies.
sources: user, notes audit, duplication audit, B2, B8

verdict.reason:
CHECKED, ALL FROM THE LIVE STORE + RUN PARTS + ENGINE SOURCE.

(1) Note lopsidedness — CONFIRMED EXACTLY. notes.json has 22 entries: branches chalebagh 19, [chalebagh,naharkhoran] 2, naharkhoran 1. Source types: 20 of 22 are `voice` (transcripts cooking-1405-05-26.txt / -05-26-02 / -06-01, all chalebagh meetings), 1 is `sheet` (F-00466, naharkhoran), 1 is `comment` (F-00465). So the branch distribution is exactly the source distribution.

(2) F-00466 vs F-00473 — CONFIRMED. F-00466 key `ashpazkhne_naharkhoran__off_ejraei__tedad_nafar_kasb_shode`, scope branches=[naharkhoran], source sheet `Ashpazkhne - Naharkhoran.xlsx` tab «OFF اجرایی» B2:D5, data.about={ref:F-00156, field:achieved_count}, field_status inferred. F-00473 key `off_ejraei__mani_do_sotoon`, scope branches=[chalebagh], source voice cooking-1405-05-26.txt line 31, data.about={ref:F-00143} and data carries literal keys `target_count` and `achieved_count`. F-00143 (chalebagh) and F-00156 (naharkhoran) are the two branch copies of the same tab record, with identical field lists [date, target_count, achieved_count, notes]. Provenance from runs/facts/cooking/20260902-080737/parts/: F-00466 came from B2, F-00473 from B8 — two different passes, as claimed. One tab's two columns are explained twice, each explanation locked to a different branch.

(3) Scale for records/rules — CONFIRMED, LARGER THAN CLAIMED. Normalising the branch/workbook token in keys (gozaresh_markazi↔gozaresh_naharkhoran, tedade_fooroosh_markazi↔_naharkhoran, anbar_markazi↔anbar_shobe_2, ashpazkhne_chalebagh↔_naharkhoran, pitza/farangi/kanter/sokhari↔amar_pitza/amar_farangi/amar_kanter/fried) yields 143 mirror clusters (70 record + 73 rule) covering 286 of 312 record+rule entries (92%). Every one of the 143 spans two different passes (B6-rules-fixed folded into B6). Store scope counts: records 73 chalebagh / 70 naharkhoran / 12 both; rules 77 / 77 / 2. The claim's 131 clusters / 126 cross-pass is the same phenomenon at a slightly stricter clustering; direction and magnitude confirmed.

(4) Pass split — CONFIRMED, and the coordinator knew. From the digest: B4 = "Gozaresh markazi" (chalebagh) non-Table tabs, B5 = its Table_* mirrors, B6 = "Gozaresh naharkhoran" non-Table tabs, B7 = its Table_* mirrors. Per-part scope is pure: B4/B5 100% chalebagh, B6/B7 100% naharkhoran. The coordinator even wrote to B6: "your error profile is identical to part B4's (the چاله‌باغ twin) ... keep the two branches structurally in step" — it recognised the twinning and still asked for no linkage.

(5) Natural key — CONFIRMED. engine/merge_facts/apply.py:277 `_natural_key = (kind, key, departments, branches)`; audit.py:668 the same. Two branch copies can never collide. It is in fact stronger than the claim: the keys themselves carry the workbook prefix (gozaresh_markazi__ vs gozaresh_naharkhoran__), so equal scope alone would still not merge them.

(6) NEW, and the part the claim misses: the design intends branch twins as two entries — spec line 442 "A value that genuinely differs per branch is two entries, each scoped to its branch. Where two branch workbooks carry the same formula, the entries are related by `template_of`" (also lines 972, 2167 "branch twins with identical formulas ... template_of + divergence"). The store has `template_of` on 0 of 486 entries, and 0 single-branch entries reference their opposite-branch twin through any ref at all. So the twins are unlinked: a copy is indistinguishable from a drift. 36 of 73 mirror rule pairs have byte-identical bodies; the other 37 "differ" only in expr style between B4 and B6 (e.g. F-00343 `(mojudi_avval_shab + daryaft_az_anbar) - mojudi_akhar_shab` vs F-00416 `masraf_elami = mojudi_avval_shab + daryaft_az_anbar - mojudi_akhar_shab`), i.e. cosmetic pass-to-pass divergence now indistinguishable from real drift. QF-43's own named example is violated: F-00322 `gozaresh_markazi__gs__jalali_to_greg` and F-00395 `gozaresh_naharkhoran__gs__jalali_to_greg` are byte-identical bodies from two .gs files, minted as two branch-scoped rules — QF-43 says such a family "yield[s] one universal rule, not four". The whole `fn__` (7) and `gs__` (10) families are duplicated this way. Only 1 entry in the entire store sits at empty scope (F-00001 `units`, the bootstrap seed) — the escape hatch was never used.

(7) No net. `merge facts audit` on the current store reports only 62 row_gone, 15 unconsumed_constant, 7 unknown_role, 4 duplicate_output — nothing about mirroring. Two reasons in engine/merge_facts/audit.py: `_lookalike_title` (line 166) skips groups whose raw values are equal (`if len(members) < 2 or len({m.get(attr) for m in members}) < 2: continue`), so the 12 byte-identical rule title pairs across branches (e.g. F-00337/F-00410 «روز تب پیتزا از تب تاریخ») pass silently; `_scope_shadow` compares a scoped entry only against an empty-scope key, never against a sibling branch. The operative prompt data-repo/.claude/agents/quantify.md mentions `template_of` once, only inside a list of ref-carrying fields (line 202), and never instructs the agent to link branch twins; line 74 just says "Assign scope by QF-43".

(8) REFUTED sub-claim: "One waste policy is split three ways across F-00470/471/472" does not evidence per-branch duplication. All three are scope chalebagh, all voice-sourced, and all three came from the SAME pass (B8). They are three distinct topics — F-00470 the two waste-registration routes (fiche vs form), F-00471 the effect of a returned dish on stock statistics, F-00472 the food-test fiche flow. That belongs to a fragmentation/granularity problem, not to P-25.

(9) Also worth noting for the redesign: QF-43 (spec line 450) literally says a transcript fact "takes the run's department" — it says nothing about branches. So for the 20 transcript notes the branch was not assigned by any rule at all; the agent inferred it from the meeting. The rule is not so much "wrong axis" as "silent on the branch axis for field material", which the agent resolved by copying the source's branch.

Severity: high is right. 286/312 record+rule entries live in unlinked branch-mirror pairs, half of them byte-identical, and 19/22 notes are branch-locked by which meeting happened to be transcribed.
verdict.corrected:
Real, high severity, but the statement needs three corrections.

CORRECTED STATEMENT: The store is branch-lopsided by source rather than by content, and nothing links or de-duplicates the branch copies.

(a) Notes — the claim is exactly right: 19/22 notes are chalebagh-only because 20 of 22 are transcript-sourced and all three transcripts read were chalebagh meetings; F-00466 (B2, sheet, naharkhoran) and F-00473 (B8, voice, chalebagh) explain the same two columns of the same «OFF اجرایی» tab, one attached to F-00156 and one to F-00143, and their keys and scopes guarantee they can never merge. QF-43 assigns only the *department* for transcript facts and is silent on branches, so the branch came from the meeting, i.e. from the source.

(b) Records and rules — the two branch copies are the DESIGNED shape, not the bug: the spec (lines 442, 972, 2167) requires one entry per branch related by `template_of` + `divergence`. The bug is that the link was never written — 0 of 486 entries carry `template_of`, and no single-branch entry references its twin by any ref — so 143 mirror clusters covering 286 of 312 record+rule entries (92%) sit in the store as flat unrelated duplicates, 36 of the 73 mirrored rule pairs with byte-identical bodies and the other 37 differing only in expr style between passes, which now reads as possible drift. On top of that, the branch-independent families (7 `fn__` + 10 `gs__` rules, including the spec's own jalali_to_greg example) were minted twice instead of once at empty scope as QF-43 requires; only 1 entry in the whole store (`units`) is at empty scope.

(c) Drop F-00470/471/472 from this problem: all three are chalebagh, voice-sourced, and from the same pass (B8), and they cover three different topics (waste routes, returned-dish effect on stock, food-test fiche). That is topical fragmentation, not per-branch duplication.

ROOT CAUSE, corrected: (1) scope is copied from the source artefact and, for field material, the branch is not specified by any rule at all, so a branch-independent definition becomes branch-local; (2) the natural key is (kind, key, departments, branches) — apply.py:277 — and the keys additionally carry the workbook prefix, so twins can never merge on either axis; (3) the improvised split put ChaleBagh (B4/B5) and Naharkhoran (B6/B7) in separate passes with 100% pure branch scope, so no pass ever saw both copies; (4) the operative prompt (quantify.md) never asks for `template_of`/`divergence` on twins even though the spec mandates it; (5) there is no detector — `merge facts audit` returns nothing on this store about mirroring, because `_lookalike_title` deliberately skips exactly-equal titles and `_scope_shadow` only compares against empty scope, never sibling branches.

title: USER COMPLAINT — colloquial transcript speech dropped verbatim into statements
description: The prompt specifies `accounts[].statement` as the home for verbatim quotes and says nothing about the register of the entry's own statement, so the quoting habit bled upward. Twelve entries carry a colloquial quote inside the primary statement and several read as meeting minutes rather than definitions. The problem is contained — it is confined to the 53 transcript-sourced entries, since rules were extracted almost entirely from sheets — but every instance is in the permanent store.
evidence: F-00301 «…(«اگه دو بسته داشته باشن خب می‌زنن ۲۰۰ گرم بعد ۲۰ گرم ۳۰ گرم باشه دوباره همونو طبق گرم می‌نویسن»)»; F-00306 «(«دو تا فکر کنم ۳۵۰، ۴۰۰ گرمیه. یا ۴۵۰ اگه اشتباه نکنم»)»; F-00479 «خود سیستم هم تلرانس در نظر می‌گیره، یعنی تو سیستم خودش حساب می‌کنه…»; F-00476 «این نیست بگیم ۱۰۰ تا تولید کن، چون خمیرمون روزانه است»; F-00464, F-00305, F-00297. B8 dispatch: 'one citing the transcript … and the speaker's words verbatim as statement'. quantify.md obligation 5: 'take every quantitative passage' with no normalisation instruction. Only 1 of 156 rule statements is affected.
root_cause: `accounts[].statement` is specified as verbatim for dispute tracking and no rule separates 'quote the source' from 'state the fact'; the entry statement is also the only place the agent has to preserve transcript colour when there is no dispute to hang an account on.
sources: user, B8, items/measurements audit, notes audit, prose audit, rules audit

verdict.reason:
COUNTS — verified against the live store (items 139, records 156, measurements 13, rules 156, notes 22 = 486 entries).

(a) Verbatim-speech quotes inside the primary `statement`: 10 entries, not 12. Exhaustive list (regex «...» spans of >=5 words, then manually separating speech from sheet-object names): F-00297, F-00301, F-00305, F-00306 (measurements), F-00464 (rule), F-00467, F-00474, F-00476, F-00479, F-00480 (notes). F-00476 carries two quotes, so 11 quote occurrences. You reach 12 only by also counting short quoted spoken phrases: F-00478 «میزان خطای مجاز» and F-00305's «یک کارتن باز»/«یک کارتن بسته». All 7 IDs cited in the evidence exist and do carry the quotes attributed to them.

(b) Containment claim is exactly right: 53 entries carry a `voice` source (notes 20, records 13, measurements 13, rules 5, items 2), and all 10 offenders are among them. Every long «...» span in a non-voice statement is a sheet tab or column name (F-00069, F-00136, F-00138, F-00154, F-00160, F-00161, F-00182, F-00239, F-00310, F-00312), never speech. No straight/curly quote characters appear in any statement in the store. The one `comment`-sourced entry (F-00465, the «149» note) is a different defect.

(c) "Only 1 of 156 rule statements" is exactly right: rules.json holds 156 entries and F-00464 is the only one.

(d) "Several read as meeting minutes" is supported and is a slightly wider set than the quote set: 'گوینده' in F-00295/F-00468/F-00476/F-00480, 'در جلسه' in F-00298/F-00300/F-00305/F-00306, 'گفته شد' in F-00305/F-00306/F-00474/F-00481. F-00295 reads as minutes («گوینده گفت گوشی خودش این فرم را بالا نمی‌آورد») with no quote at all.

ROOT CAUSE — the first half is wrong. quantify.md does NOT specify `accounts[].statement` as verbatim: grep for 'verbatim' in /data-repo/.claude/agents/quantify.md hits only lines 49, 71, 80, 114, 164, 209, none about accounts, and the only line mentioning `accounts[].statement` (187) is the Persian/ASCII rule. facts-delta.schema.json has NO description on either `$defs/account/properties/statement` or `$defs/envelope/properties/statement` — both are bare `{"type":"string"}`. The verbatim/own-words distinction exists ONLY in the design spec, lines 538-544: "`statement` is the entry's explanation — a Persian sentence or short paragraph in the agent's own words... It is distinct from `accounts[].statement`, which holds *verbatim quotes* from sources." The agent never receives that file — its documented inputs are department, run_dir, transcripts, dumps, images, scripts, processes, facts_index, schema_path, data_root. quantify.md line 71 claims the nine obligations are "Transcribed from the spec verbatim", but QF-4's own-words rule was never transcribed at all. The rule was designed and then lost between spec and prompt.

The second half of the root cause is right, and I confirmed the bleed vector in the B8 dispatch (read from the raw jsonl, not the truncated digest): 'one citing the transcript (`type: "voice"`, with `lines` and the speaker's words verbatim as `statement`, plus `speaker_role`...)' and, in the Return section, '**every disputed field with both its accounts verbatim**'. Two 'verbatim' instructions, both about accounts, with nothing anywhere telling the agent the entry's own statement must be its own words.

AGGRAVATOR NOT IN THE CLAIM: `statement` is in PROSE_LEAVES (engine/merge_facts/ladder.py:6-7) and the ladder at lines 161-165 fills it only when empty, then `continue  # never disputed, never rewritten`. A corrected re-run of quantify cannot repair these 10 statements; each needs a targeted `edit-fact` delta. That is what makes "every instance is in the permanent store" actually bite.

SEVERITY — overstated. 10/486 = 2.1% of entries, split notes 5 / measurements 4 / rules 1; zero effect on any value, unit, key, ref, or validation outcome (B8 contributed 12 validation errors, none register-related); in 7 of the 10 the quote is appended to an otherwise own-words statement rather than replacing it. The prompt fix is one sentence; cleanup is 10 edit-fact runs. Medium, not high.
verdict.corrected:
USER COMPLAINT — colloquial transcript speech dropped verbatim into statements. Real, contained, medium severity. Ten entries carry a verbatim speech quote inside the primary `statement` (eleven quote occurrences; twelve if two short quoted spoken phrases are counted): F-00297, F-00301, F-00305, F-00306 (measurements), F-00464 (rule), F-00467, F-00474, F-00476, F-00479, F-00480 (notes). A wider set of about eleven entries reads as meeting minutes rather than definitions ('گوینده گفت', 'در جلسه گفته شد', 'نمونه‌ای که گفته شد'), F-00295 being the clearest case with no quote at all. The problem is exactly confined to the 53 voice-sourced entries — every long «...» span in a non-voice statement is a sheet tab or column name — and only 1 of 156 rule statements is affected, because rules came almost entirely from sheets.

Root cause: the design spec DOES carry the rule (lines 538-544: `statement` is "a Persian sentence or short paragraph in the agent's own words", explicitly "distinct from `accounts[].statement`, which holds *verbatim quotes* from sources"), but it was never transcribed into the agent prompt. quantify.md never uses the word verbatim about either statement field, and facts-delta.schema.json gives both `statement` fields a bare `{"type":"string"}` with no description — while the file the agent is told to treat as authoritative is the schema, not the spec. The B8 dispatch then pushed the habit the other way twice, both times about accounts ('the speaker's words verbatim as `statement`', 'both its accounts verbatim'), with no counterweight. Aggravating factor: `statement` is a PROSE_LEAVES field (engine/merge_facts/ladder.py:161-165) — filled once, never rewritten — so a re-run with a fixed prompt cannot repair the ten; each needs its own edit-fact delta.

title: Statements are fill-in-the-blank boilerplate — the store is a second copy of the spreadsheet
description: Where an entry's real content lives entirely in `data`, the required prose field has nothing left to carry and becomes a template. All 139 item statements are one of two templates whose only variable content is which tab of which file the item's column sits in; 51 of B1's 52 items use one sentence; 69 of B3's 87 items collapse to 7 templates. Twelve reference records reproduce 1,015 hand-typed BOM cells that a 12 KB TSV already contains, verified transcription-error-free — deterministic work done by an LLM through a 64K output budget.
evidence: 167 of 486 entries (34%) sit in a boilerplate cluster. F-00002…F-00007 repeat one sentence with the name and code swapped. B3: 69 `dish_*` items with the identical four data keys and 7 statement templates. B7: the fragment «تنها یک فرمول در A1 دارد که با IMPORT_FROM_SHEET محدوده» appears verbatim in 35 of 35 mirror statements = 19% of all its statement characters. F-00167…F-00178: 76,654 B, 1,015 cells of which 583 are literal zeros, all verified identical to rows.tsv (0 mismatches). `bindings` is 318 per-cell entries = 9.6% of rules.json, duplicating what source[] and the target record already hold.
root_cause: A required prose field with nothing to carry becomes boilerplate, and obligation 2 makes the LLM the emitter of mechanical JSON. No engine verb turns a dumped tab into a record skeleton, so every mechanical field (key, location, column letters, import args, named_range, locators) is spent as generated tokens.
sources: prose audit, B1, B3, B5, B7, records audit, dump audit

verdict.reason:
CHECKED EVERY FIGURE. Verdict: problem REAL, root cause CORRECT on all three legs, several evidence numbers OVERSTATED.

== CONFIRMED EXACTLY ==
1. `statement` required on all five kinds: code-repo/schemas/facts-delta.schema.json line 77-78 `"required": ["kind","key","title","statement","scope","source","retired","data"]`; spec 2026-08-29-quantitative-facts-design.md:538 "`statement` is the entry's explanation — a Persian sentence or short paragraph in the agent's own words, required on every kind".
2. Obligation 2 assigns mechanical transcription to the LLM. data-repo/.claude/agents/quantify.md lines 72-88: "Walk each workbook dump: per non-empty tab one `record` ... a BOM or dictionary tab gets `role: reference` and its `rows.tsv` cells as `rows[]` ... per `#N`/`##N` code found in a header or in the row-label column of a BOM tab an item".
3. No engine skeleton verb. `merge facts` subcommands (engine/merge/cli.py:200-228): apply, resolve, retire, promote, repair-foreign-keys, repair-source-refs, export, revert (+audit/check/coverage). engine/dump_workbook/cli.py emits sheets.json/rows.tsv only. Nothing generates a record or item skeleton.
4. B1 = 52 items, B3 = 87 items (runs/facts/cooking/20260902-080737/parts/facts-delta-B1.json, -B3.json). 51 of B1's 52 items carry the «قلم انبارگردانی» sentence shape.
5. All 69 `dish_*` items in B3 carry the IDENTICAL data key set (category, code, unit, unit_ref) — 69/69, no exceptions.
6. F-00167…F-00178 = 12 reference records, `rows[]` holds exactly 1,015 numeric cells, 583 of them literal 0 in the store (571 in the B3 delta). rows.tsv for that workbook (.dump/15M2ovUmBvK3AMzGxeq-ijwE_KOQBjOZakLvQCs-eE10/rows.tsv) = 12,406 B. I re-ran the transcription check independently (map field key item_N -> item code ##N -> rows.tsv union-header column, 69 rows): 1,000 of 1,015 cells compared, 0 mismatches, 0 unmapped rows; the 15 uncompared are fields whose item has no ## code (e.g. «پنیر پیتزا میکس»). Transcription is error-free, as claimed.
7. `bindings`: 318 per-cell entries across 41 rules in facts/rules.json — exact. Sample F-00340 bindings are {row: item_N, cell: E6..E15, ingredient_id: N} — derivable from the target record's field order + column letter + start row, i.e. mechanical.

== OVERSTATED / WRONG ==
A. "All 139 item statements are one of two templates whose only variable content is which tab of which file" — WRONG. Four families, not two: آیتم منوی 68, قلم انبارگردانی 51, قلم مواد اولیه 11, قلم بسته‌بندی 7, other 2. After aggressive normalisation (title/aliases/quoted names/codes/filenames/digits blanked) the 139 items yield 66 distinct templates, largest covering 14. Variable content is not only the tab/file: it includes the production line or menu family, the unit, the BASIS for inferring the unit, and 38 distinct trailing clauses recording real per-item anomalies (column empty at extraction time, header missing the ## prefix, row values duplicate another row, code collision on two dishes, stray leading space).
B. "51 of B1's 52 items use one sentence" — true only at family level. Literally those 51 resolve to 22 distinct normalised templates; the largest covers 14 of 52 (27%).
C. "69 of B3's 87 items collapse to 7 templates" — near. By first-sentence clusters there are 12 clusters and the top 7 cover 61 of 69 (not 69). Normalising away the family word collapses all 69 to 1 template, so the spirit holds, the count does not.
D. "the fragment appears verbatim in 35 of 35 mirror statements = 19% of all its statement characters" — WRONG twice. It appears in 35 of B7's 50 records (all 50 are mirror-related, only 35 use that phrasing). Measured share = 11.8% of B7's 16,353 record-statement characters, or 15.3% if measured only across the 35 that contain it. Never 19%. Store-wide the fragment appears in 70 records = the same 35 mirrors written once for chalebagh and once for naharkhoran (35+35), which is a duplication finding, not a B7 finding.
E. "76,654 B" — the 12 records are 77,338 B compact in the store, 72,618 B in the B3 delta; 76,654 B matches nothing (it is 1 B off facts-delta-B2.json's file size, 76,655 B — likely a copy error). Also, only 20,883 B of the 72,618 B is `rows[]` itself; 22,389 B is `fields[]`, 4,988 B `field_status`, 6,877 B statements. So "76 KB reproducing a 12 KB TSV" overstates: ~21 KB is the cell copy.
F. "`bindings` = 9.6% of rules.json" — WRONG. 6.5% measured compact, 14.7% measured on the file as actually stored (pretty-printed, indent 2). 9.6% matches neither.
G. "167 of 486 entries (34%) in a boilerplate cluster" — my measure: 156/486 = 32% share a normalised statement template with at least one other entry (86 = 18% at cluster size >=3). Within normalisation noise; defensible.

== BONUS CORROBORATION (not in the claim) ==
10 of the 12 BOM record statements assert «سلول صفر ... در rows نیامده است» (zero cells are not carried in rows) while 571 zeros are in fact present in those same rows[]. The boilerplate sentence contradicts the data it labels — direct evidence that the required prose is a template, not a description.

== SEVERITY ==
High is defensible on cost (deterministic copy work spent through a 64K output budget, and the 64K crashes are the same budget), but the headline "the store is a second copy of the spreadsheet" is only literally true for the 12 reference records. The templated item prose does carry something the sheet does not state (unit + inference basis + per-item anomaly), so it is boilerplate with a thin payload, not pure duplication. High on cost/effort, medium on data-value harm.
verdict.corrected: P-27 (corrected). Where an entry's real content lives entirely in `data`, the required prose field has little left to carry and degenerates into a template with a thin payload. The 139 item statements fall into four families (menu item 68, inventory item 51, raw material 11, packaging 7) and 66 distinct normalised templates; the variable content is the line/menu family, the tab and file, the unit, the basis for inferring the unit, and one of 38 short anomaly clauses. 51 of B1's 52 items share one sentence shape (22 distinct templates, largest covering 14). All 69 of B3's `dish_*` items carry the identical four data keys (category, code, unit, unit_ref) and collapse to a single template once the family word is treated as a slot (top-7 first-sentence clusters cover 61 of 69). In B7, the fragment «تنها یک فرمول در A1 دارد که با IMPORT_FROM_SHEET محدوده» appears verbatim in 35 of its 50 records = 11.8% of its record-statement characters (15.3% across the 35 that contain it); store-wide it appears 70 times because the same 35 mirrors are written once per branch. Twelve reference records (F-00167…F-00178, 72.6 KB in the delta / 77.3 KB in the store, of which 20.9 KB is `rows[]`) hand-transcribe 1,015 BOM cells — 583 of them literal zeros — that a 12,406 B rows.tsv already contains; an independent re-check maps 1,000 of the 1,015 back to rows.tsv with 0 mismatches, so the transcription is error-free deterministic work done by an LLM through a 64K output budget. Ten of those twelve statements nonetheless assert that zero cells are omitted from `rows[]` while 571 zeros sit in them. `bindings` is 318 per-cell entries across 41 rules (6.5% of rules.json compact, 14.7% as stored) that restate what the column letter, the start row and the target record's field order already fix. About 156 of 486 entries (32%) share a statement template with another entry. Root cause as stated and verified: `statement` is required on all five kinds (facts-delta.schema.json envelope required list; design spec line 538), obligation 2 of quantify.md makes the LLM the emitter of mechanical JSON ("its `rows.tsv` cells as `rows[]`", "per ##N code ... an item"), and no engine verb turns a dumped tab into a record or item skeleton (`merge facts` has apply/resolve/retire/promote/repair-*/export/revert only; `dump-workbook` stops at the TSVs). Severity: high on cost, medium on data-value harm — only the 12 reference records are literally a second copy of the spreadsheet.

title: Pipeline jargon and extraction meta-commentary leak into user-facing Persian prose
description: A third of statements narrate the agent's own bookkeeping rather than the fact: why an expression could not be written, that the original text is stored elsewhere, that this pass does not define something, that a value was recorded as an account. Latin identifiers are pervasive — workbook filenames, A1 refs, mirror-tab names, spreadsheet functions and schema field names — inside prose that a restaurant owner is meant to read. Batch-run vocabulary («در این پاس») was written into 30 permanent store entries.
evidence: 52 of 486 statements (33%) carry housekeeping: «متن اصلی در original آمده» ×30, «این پاس آن را تعریف نمی‌کند» ×19, «در bindings آمده است» ×15, «در زیرمجموعه FEEL بیان‌پذیر نیست» ×13. 442 of 486 entries (91%) carry a non-allowed Latin token; 1,810 occurrences of 223 distinct tokens (Mavade/Avalie.xlsx 125 each, A1 77, IMPORT_FROM_SHEET 74, Table_* 218). Jargon: `bindings` 15, `FEEL` 15, `rows` 10, `account` 5 (e.g. «هر سه عدد به‌عنوان account ثبت شده است»). F-00311 even asks a human to merge the duplicate it just wrote.
root_cause: There is no separation between the fact and the extraction log, so the excuse lands in the user-facing field; and the only language rule says the field must be Persian, without marking the pipeline's own vocabulary as internal. The coordinator explicitly requested some of it ('drop expr and keep the verbatim original, saying in one sentence in statement why').
sources: prose audit, rules audit, B6, B7, coordinator

verdict.reason:
Re-derived every figure from the store (486 entries across items/records/measurements/rules/notes.json) and confirmed the mechanism in the schema, prompt, spec, engine and coordinator transcript.

CONFIRMED — housekeeping prose (counts are entries, not occurrences, over `statement`):
- «در bindings آمده است» — 15 (exact match to claim)
- FEEL-inexpressibility excuse (statement contains both `FEEL` and «بیان») — 13 (exact match)
- «این پاس …تعریف نمی‌کند» — 18 (claim 19); any «این پاس» — 49; «در این پاس» — 31 (claim 30)
- «متن اصلی» — 33; of those, 7 name the field `original` literally (claim's «متن اصلی در original آمده» ×30 splits the difference: 33 say "the original text is elsewhere", 7 use the Latin field name)
- jargon `rows` 10, `account` 5 — both exact. F-00055/F-00057/F-00305/F-00306 literally read «هر دو خوانش به‌عنوان account ثبت شده است».
- F-00311 confirmed verbatim: «…و در صورت تأیید انسان می‌توان دو مورد را ادغام کرد.» — the entry asks a human to merge the duplicate it just wrote.

CONFIRMED — Latin leakage, reproduced almost exactly (the claimant clearly counted `statement`+`title`): 442/486 entries (90.9%) carry ≥1 Latin token; 1,830 occurrences of 226 distinct tokens (claim: 1,810/223). Top tokens: Mavade 125, Avalie.xlsx 125, A1 77, Gozaresh 71, IMPORT_FROM_SHEET 72 (claim 74), markazi.xlsx 66, naharkhoran.xlsx 57. `Table_*` appears 148 times inside statements (133 entries) — the claim's 218 is the one figure I could not reproduce at any field scope (662 across whole entry JSON), but the phenomenon is real and pervasive.

MIS-STATED — the headline: "52 of 486 statements (33%)" is internally inconsistent (52/486 = 10.7%) and both halves are wrong. The union of the four cited phrase families is 79 entries = 16.3% of the store (a broader bookkeeping filter adds «خوانده نشده»/«ثبت نشده» and reaches 96 = 19.8%). "A third" is true only of one kind: 49/156 rules = 31.4%; records 30/156 = 19.2%; items/measurements/notes carry essentially none (the `account` cases only).

ROOT CAUSE — all three legs verified:
1. No separation between fact and extraction log. code-repo/schemas/facts-delta.schema.json `$defs/envelope` has no internal/agent-notes field; the only escape hatch, `issues[]`, is enum-typed to data-quality kinds (scale, unit_kind, column_shift, junk, bug, cross_record, code_collision) — "I could not write a FEEL expr" and "this pass did not read the file" have nowhere to go but `statement`.
2. The only language rule is "must be Persian": data-repo/.claude/agents/quantify.md:187-191 (QF-32 "Persian values, ASCII structure"). grep for audience/reader/jargon/خواننده/مالک across agents/quantify.md and skills/quantify/SKILL.md returns nothing — no rule marks pipeline vocabulary as internal, and none forbids workbook filenames or A1 refs in prose.
3. The coordinator explicitly requested it — verbatim, in the B6 fix SendMessage at 2026-09-02T18:52:15Z (transcript ffa1efdd…jsonl): "where the formula truly is not expressible in the FEEL subset — **drop `expr` and keep the verbatim `original`**, saying in one sentence in `statement` why." The B6 subagent reported back "each with a sentence in `statement` saying why" (64 rules rewritten); the B4 subagent the same ("each such rule's `statement` now says in one sentence why no FEEL expression is given", 13 rules).

SEVERITY high stands, and one fact strengthens it that the claim omits: `statement` is write-once. Spec §11 QF-17 and engine/merge_facts/ladder.py:161-164 (`PROSE_LEAVES` → fill-if-empty, "never disputed, never rewritten") mean a later run cannot repair any of these 79 statements; only a manual `edit-fact` can. And the prose is genuinely user-facing: ui/src/facts/FactDetail.tsx:150 renders `entry.statement` in the Persian end-user app (alongside a FactConfirm screen), even though the spec (line 538) frames its audience as "the first thing a reviewer reads" rather than the owner — so the claim's "prose a restaurant owner is meant to read" is right about where it lands but slightly overstates what the spec intended.
verdict.corrected: Pipeline jargon and extraction meta-commentary leak into the permanent, user-facing Persian `statement` field. 79 of 486 store entries (16%) narrate the agent's own bookkeeping rather than the fact — concentrated in rules (49/156 = 31%, hence "a third of rules", not a third of the store) and records (30/156 = 19%): «متن اصلی … در original آمده» ×33, «در این پاس …» ×31 (18 of them «این پاس آن را تعریف نمی‌کند»), «در bindings آمده است» ×15, «در زیرمجموعه FEEL بیان‌پذیر نیست» ×13, plus «به‌عنوان account ثبت شده است» ×5. Latin identifiers are pervasive: 442 of 486 entries (91%) carry a Latin token in title or statement — 1,830 occurrences of 226 distinct tokens (Mavade 125, Avalie.xlsx 125, A1 77, IMPORT_FROM_SHEET 72, Table_* 148 in statements across 133 entries). F-00311 asks a human to merge the duplicate it just wrote. Three causes, all verified: (a) the delta schema's envelope has no field for extraction meta and `issues[]` is enum-typed to data-quality kinds, so the excuse lands in the user-facing field; (b) the agent prompt's only language rule (QF-32, quantify.md:187) says the field must be Persian and nothing marks pipeline vocabulary or workbook/A1 identifiers as internal; (c) the coordinator explicitly ordered it during the fix rounds ("drop `expr` and keep the verbatim `original`, saying in one sentence in `statement` why"). Severity is high and the damage is permanent: `statement` is a write-once prose field (spec §11 QF-17, engine/merge_facts/ladder.py:161) that no re-run can overwrite — only a manual `edit-fact` can clean these 79 entries.

title: The content an ERP actually needs is the content that is missing
description: While the mechanical walk completed, the three edges the spec calls the ERP builder's real inheritance are used zero times, no item carries pack structure, and the highest-value payload in the estate — the BOM — is only partially extracted. Sixteen reference records hold 85 rows where the spec says the BOM alone is ~1,200 cells, and coverage reports 13 of 28 workbooks. The pack facts do exist in the store, scattered as measurements and notes, because there was no item field in front of the agent to put them in.
evidence: `foreignKeys` 0/156 records, `reconciled_against` 0/156, `template_of` 0/156 rules. `units[]` 0/139 items, `pack` 0/139, `tracked` 0/139, `place` category 0, `movement` 0. `merge facts check`: coverage 13 of 28 workbooks, 15 uncited_workbook. Meanwhile F-00302 (pasta 1.2 kg pack, 5 portions), F-00304 (30-slice bacon pack 900–980 g), F-00305 (200–300 gouda slices/carton), F-00484 (40 kg flour pack) sit as measurements and notes. Spec §9: 'the report multiplies single-pizza dough by 1 where the BOM says 180 g, and without this edge nothing can surface it'.
root_cause: The mechanical walk is uniform — a mirror tab and a 1,200-cell BOM cost the same in the obligation list but 100× the output tokens — so under an output ceiling the cheap obligations complete and the expensive one truncates. The valuable edges are optional fields absent from the prompt's numbered obligations (P-16).
sources: consumer audit, records audit, items/measurements audit, B3, input-shape

verdict.reason:
CONFIRMED (field census over data-repo/facts/*.json, entries=139 item / 156 record / 13 measurement / 156 rule / 22 note):
- `foreignKeys` 0/156 records, `reconciled_against` 0/156 records, `template_of` 0/156 rules — the key never appears in any entry's `data`.
- `units[]` 0/139, `pack` 0/139, `tracked` 0/139 items; `movement` 0; category `place` 0.
- Prompt absence verified by grep over data-repo/.claude/agents/quantify.md + skills/quantify/: `reconciled_against`, `item.pack`, `units[]`, `pack_unit`, `factor_to_base`, `movement` = ZERO hits anywhere. `foreignKeys` appears only as a prohibition (quantify.md:87-89). `template_of` appears once (quantify.md:202) only as an example of a `{ref}` envelope, never as an obligation. So P-16's "absent from the numbered obligations" is right for those.
- Counter-nuance: `item.tracked` IS named in obligation 5 (quantify.md:99) and is still 0/139, so prompt omission is not the whole mechanism.
- Concrete instances that should have carried the edges: F-00332 `gozaresh_markazi__pitza__tolerance__item_1` (5 g) and F-00405 `gozaresh_naharkhoran__pitza__tolerance__item_1` (5 g) are the same constant in the two report workbooks with no `template_of` — exactly the case spec line 972 names ("the Naharkhoran report's are template_of instances"). F-00169 `mavade_avalie__pitza_single` carries `item_26: 180` (dough 180 g) with no `reconciled_against` — exactly §9's example. 23 distinct `expr` strings are shared by 68 rules with zero `template_of` links (incl. `convert_gr_to_kg` = `weight / 1000` duplicated across the two report workbooks).
- F-00302 (1.2 kg pasta pack, `portions_per_pack` 5, `gram_per_portion` 240), F-00304 (`pack_size` 30, range 900–980 g), F-00305 (200–300 gouda slices/carton), F-00484 (40 kg flour, "مانده آن ثبت نمی‌شود" = a `tracked` exception) all exist as measurements/notes, not as item payload. Claim holds.
- Extra finding the claim misses: the agent invented an item `category` vocabulary entirely outside the spec's enum (spec:761 `ingredient|product|packaging|consumable|place|other`; store: dairy 6, meat 22, sauce 3, dough 1, vegetable 8, bread 4, pasta 1, prepared 3, beverage 14, oil 1, packaging 7, menu_item 69). quantify.md:265 lists `category` as required with no enum, facts-delta.schema.json leaves `data` free-form, and merge_facts/verbs.py:81 only checks presence. `place` is 0 because the whole axis was replaced, not because one value was skipped.

REFUTED:
1. "the BOM is only partially extracted; sixteen reference records hold 85 rows where the spec says ~1,200 cells". The BOM source (dump 15M2ovUmBvK3AMzGxeq-ijwE_KOQBjOZakLvQCs-eE10, sheets.json) is 12 tabs = 69 data rows / 1,015 data cells; rows.tsv is 70 lines (header + 69). The store's 12 `mavade_avalie__*` reference records hold exactly 69 rows and 1,084 value cells, byte-matching rows.tsv (spot-checked dish_71: 180,80,0,0,0,0,0,0,230,0,0,0,20,0,8,0,1,1). The BOM is 100% extracted. The evidence conflates rows with cells — 85 is the ROW count across 18 (not 16) reference records, and the cells live inline on those rows. The spec's own "~1,200 cells" was an estimate of 1,015.
2. "coverage reports 13 of 28 workbooks / 15 uncited_workbook" as evidence of missing content. attachments/sheets/manifest.json assigns exactly 13 workbooks to `cooking`; the 15 uncited are exactly the 15 non-cooking workbooks (preparation, warehouse x3, management, accounting, logistics x2, cashier x4, dining x2, procurement). The cooking run read 13/13 of its scope. merge_facts/audit.py:851 `coverage()` counts the whole manifest by design ("QF-44's readiness test reads it"), so it is estate-wide readiness, not per-run coverage. Also 38/38 reference_tabs declared on cooking workbooks have a record (checked programmatically, 0 missing).
3. Root cause "the mechanical walk is uniform ... under an output ceiling the cheap obligations complete and the expensive one truncates". Contradicted by (1): the single most expensive obligation in the estate — the 1,084-cell BOM — is the one thing that completed in full, while cheap optional edges are the ones at zero. The prompt-omission half of the root cause survives; the truncation half does not.

SEVERITY: claimed high, actual medium. Two of the four evidence legs are false and the estate's stated highest-value payload is fully present. Most of what is missing is recoverable from data already in the store without re-reading the estate (template_of is a mechanical pairing of already-stored identical exprs; pack facts already carry pack_size/portions_per_pack on measurements and need reshaping, not re-extraction). Only `reconciled_against` and `foreignKeys` need a fresh read of the report formulas.
verdict.corrected:
The structural edges and the item payload axes the spec designed for the ERP builder are unused: `foreignKeys` 0/156 records, `reconciled_against` 0/156, `template_of` 0/156 rules, `units[]`/`pack`/`tracked` 0/139 items, `movement` 0. The pack and tracking content exists but is scattered as measurements and notes (F-00302, F-00304, F-00305, F-00484) because no item field was in front of the agent. Separately, the agent invented an item `category` vocabulary outside the spec's enum (dairy, meat, menu_item, ... instead of ingredient|product|packaging|consumable|place|other), which is why `place` is 0; neither the schema nor `merge facts apply` constrains it. Root cause is prompt omission, not output truncation: `reconciled_against`, `item.pack`, `units[]`, `pack_unit`, `factor_to_base` and `movement` appear nowhere in the quantify prompt, `foreignKeys` appears only as a prohibition, and `template_of` only as a `{ref}`-envelope example — none are numbered obligations. But `item.tracked` IS a numbered obligation (quantify.md:99) and is still 0/139, so naming a field in the prompt is necessary and not sufficient.

The two coverage claims are wrong and should be dropped. The BOM is fully extracted, not partially: its 12 tabs hold 69 data rows / 1,015 cells and the store's 12 `mavade_avalie__*` records hold 69 rows / 1,084 cells matching rows.tsv verbatim; "85 rows" was a row count read as a cell count. And `coverage: 13 of 28` is 13/13 of the workbooks the manifest assigns to `cooking` — the 15 uncited ones are exactly the 15 other departments' workbooks, and `coverage()` is estate-wide readiness by design. Because the most expensive obligation completed in full while the cheap optional edges are at zero, the "output ceiling truncates the expensive obligation" root cause is contradicted. Severity: medium — template_of and the pack reshaping are derivable from what the store already holds; only `reconciled_against` and `foreignKeys` need a fresh read of the report formulas.

title: The `measurement` kind is wholly misused: all 13 entries are misfiled constants
description: The spec defines `data.quantity` as a kind-of-quantity enum and the kind itself as 'what is captured, by whom, into which record field'. Every stored measurement instead puts a number in `quantity`, and none carries `by`, `when` or `writes_to` — so the who/when/into-which-field knowledge the kind exists for is absent from the store entirely, while all 13 entries are values stated singly, which the classification ladder routes to a constant rule. The UI types the field as the enum and renders it through a label map, so it shows a lookup miss on all 13.
evidence: data.quantity values: 30, null, 110, 285, 200, 100, 1.2, 200, null, null, 450, 10, null — 0/13 on the enum. `by` 0/13, `when` 0/13, `writes_to` 0/13, `method` 1/13. F-00469 (a NOTE) carries exactly the measurement payload: start 01:15, by سرلاین, method وزن‌گیری, targeting four records. Schema requires only `[quantity, unit]` present, with no enum. ui/src/api/types.ts:305 types it as the enum; MeasurementCard renders via QUANTITY_LABELS.
root_cause: The schema checks key presence, never value, so `validate` cannot push back; and the kind's name reads as 'a measurement = a measured number', a reading nothing in the prompt contradicts. §8's rule 8 vs rule 11 distinction is stated only in the spec.
sources: items/measurements audit, notes audit, consumer audit

verdict.reason:
CONFIRMED, with one refinement (1 of the 13 is a legitimate measurement per the spec's own acceptance fixture, but its payload is wrong too).

STORE (data-repo/facts/measurements.json, 13 entries total, all departments):
- data.quantity values in file order: F-00296=30, F-00297=null, F-00298=110, F-00299=285, F-00300=200, F-00301=100, F-00302=1.2, F-00303=200, F-00304=null, F-00305=null, F-00306=450, F-00307=10, F-00308=null. Enum hits ({mass,count,volume,duration,money,ratio,other}) = 0/13. Exactly as claimed.
- key presence: quantity 13/13, unit 13/13, of 10/13, per 11/13, range 6/13, method 1/13 (F-00296 only), writes_to 0/13, when 0/13, by 0/13, exceptions 0/13. Exactly as claimed.
- source types: 13/13 carry a `voice` (transcript) source; 2 also cite a sheet, 1 a process. Every measurement in the store came out of a transcript pass, none out of a workbook pass.
- `writes_to` appears 108 times in rules.json (rule outputs) and 0 times in measurements.json — the agent used the field freely elsewhere, so this is not ignorance of the key, it is a wrong reading of the kind.

SPEC (code-repo/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-29-quantitative-facts-design.md):
- L928 heading: "### `measurement` — what is captured, by whom, into which record field"; L930 "Required: `quantity`, `unit`"; L935 example `"quantity": "mass", "unit": "g"` with method/when/by/writes_to/exceptions; L943 "`quantity`: `mass | count | volume | duration | money | ratio | other`". Enum confirmed.
- §8 ladder L1094-1111: rule 8 "Is a value stated singly — a literal in a formula, a number in a sentence → **`rule` with no inputs** (a constant)"; rule 11 "Says who captures what, when, into which field → **`measurement`**". Confirmed.
- DECISIVE: the spec's own cooking acceptance fixture (L2044-2052) names the expected output for this exact department and lists as **constants**: `cooked_to_raw_factor_grilled_chicken` (=F-00296), `drip_loss_g_per_kg_steak` (=F-00297), `chicken_g_per_portion_crispy` 285/265-310 (=F-00299), `pack_g_penne` 1200 (=F-00302), `portion_g_penne` 240, `pack_g_parmesan` 100 with supersedes the 200 (=F-00301/F-00300), `oil_loss_l_per_night` range 8-12 (=F-00308). All seven are stored as measurements. The fixture names exactly ONE measurement: "`item` · `bacon` with `units[].factor_to_base` a range (30 slices = 900-980 g) and a `measurement` of `quantity: mass` on it" (=F-00304) — so F-00304's existence as a measurement is correct, but it stores `{quantity: null, unit: g, range: [900,980], pack_size: 30}` instead of `quantity: "mass"`, and the 900-980 g range is on the measurement rather than on item F-00022's `units[].factor_to_base` (F-00022.data = `{category, unit: kg, unit_ref, code: ##15}` — no `units[]` at all).
- F-00469 (note) confirmed: data = `{start_time: "01:15", about: [F-00147, F-00149, F-00151, F-00153]}`, and F-00147/149/151/153 are exactly the four «موجودی آخر شب» records (pizza/farangi/counter/sokhari, chalebagh). The statement carries "سرلاین هر بخش موظف است همه اقلام را وزن‌گیری کند". So the who/when/into-which-record content is present in the store — as a note, in Persian prose, not as `by`/`when`/`writes_to` fields. Small correction to the evidence wording: the note does not "carry the measurement payload" as fields, it carries it as prose plus `about[]`.

SCHEMA (code-repo/schemas/facts-delta.schema.json): measurement branch is `{"data": {"type":"object","required":["quantity","unit"],"properties":{"of":{...}}}}` — no type, no enum on `quantity`, `additionalProperties` unset. Root cause 1 confirmed. Also confirmed by grep: `quantity` and `measurement` appear ZERO times in engine/validate/*.py and engine/merge_facts/content.py — there is no content check on the field anywhere. The only engine mentions are engine/merge_facts/verbs.py:83 (`"measurement": ("quantity","unit")`, promote's required-key map) and the test fixtures (tests/test_merge_facts_apply.py:112, :395, test_merge_facts_revert.py:73, test_merge_facts_audit.py:494-496), which all write `"quantity": "mass"` — the enum reading is in the authors' fixtures but enforced nowhere.

PROMPT (data-repo/.claude/agents/quantify.md, 293 lines; skills/quantify/SKILL.md, 675 lines): root cause 2 and 3 confirmed and stronger than claimed.
- The ONLY measurement guidance in the prompt is the table at quantify.md:267 — `| measurement | quantity, unit |`. The spec's kind definition ("what is captured, by whom, into which record field"), the `mass|count|...` enum, and the `by`/`when`/`writes_to`/`method`/`exceptions` fields do not appear anywhere in either prompt file.
- quantify.md:104 says "Classify with §8 in order" but the §8 ladder text is not in either file (grep for "first match"/"stated singly"/"who captures" returns nothing), and neither file gives a path to the spec — the agent is told to obey a section it was never handed.
- quantify.md:98 (obligation 5, transcripts) actively pushes the numeric reading: "Read each chosen transcript in full and take every quantitative passage: measurements, constants (value or range, unit, `per`, `of`, `valid_from`), rules …" — "measurements" heads the list of quantitative passages and shares the parenthetical field list (`unit`, `per`, `of`) that the 13 stored entries actually use. This is the single strongest cause: every stored measurement is a transcript number, and this line is the one place the prompt uses the word.
- quantify.md:252 tells the agent the schema file is "authoritative on the exact shape" — and the schema, as shown, permits a number.

ENGINE, extra evidence not in the claim: merge_facts/apply.py:167 `_measurement_key` returns None unless `data.of` AND `data.writes_to.field` are both present, so with 0/13 `writes_to` the spec's canonical measurement key `{item.key}__{record.key}__{column.key}` (spec L378) was never derived once — all 13 kept the agent's advisory minted key, silently, via the escape hatch the spec meant for "a measurement that writes nowhere (a verbal report)" (L943-944).

UI (code-repo/ui): types.ts:306 (claim said 305 — off by one, 305 is the interface line) types `quantity` as the 7-member enum; MeasurementCard.tsx:37 renders `label(QUANTITY_LABELS, d.quantity)`; factsLabels.ts:784-792 `label()` throws `new Error("factsLabels: no Persian label for «…»")` when `import.meta.env.DEV`, else returns the raw value. Precise consequence: the 9 numeric entries throw on a dev build and render the bare number ("30 · percent", "1.2 · kg") on a production build; the 4 null entries return '' and render just " · g". Separately, on all 13 the «زمان · توسط» pane renders "— · —" via `none()` and the «ثبت در» pane renders empty — half the card is dead for every entry in the store.

SEVERITY: high is right. The kind is 100% unusable as designed, the knowledge it exists to hold is absent from the store (or stranded in note prose), the spec's own acceptance fixture for this department is failed on at least 7 named rows, and no layer — schema, validate, merge, prompt — could catch it.
verdict.corrected: The `measurement` kind is misused on every one of its 13 entries, but not identically. Payload: 0/13 put a kind-of-quantity on `data.quantity` — all 13 put a number or null there (30, null, 110, 285, 200, 100, 1.2, 200, null, null, 450, 10, null) — and 0/13 carry `by`, `when` or `writes_to` (1/13 carries `method`), so the who/when/into-which-record knowledge the kind exists for is absent from the store; where it survives at all it is Persian prose in a note (F-00469: `data.start_time` 01:15 + `about[]` pointing at the four «موجودی آخر شب» records, with «سرلاین … وزن‌گیری» only in the statement). Classification: 12 of the 13 are values stated singly that §8 rule 8 routes to a constant rule — and the spec's own cooking acceptance fixture (L2044-2050) names seven of them as constants by key (`cooked_to_raw_factor_grilled_chicken`, `drip_loss_g_per_kg_steak`, `chicken_g_per_portion_crispy`, `pack_g_penne`, `portion_g_penne`, `pack_g_parmesan` + its superseded 200, `oil_loss_l_per_night`). The exception is F-00304 (bacon), which the same fixture explicitly wants as "a `measurement` of `quantity: mass`" — its existence is correct, its payload is not (`quantity: null` plus a `range: [900,980]` that the fixture puts on item `bacon`'s `units[].factor_to_base`, where F-00022 has no `units[]` at all). Root cause as stated, plus three: (a) the prompt never contains the ladder it invokes — quantify.md:104 says "Classify with §8 in order" while §8's text and the kind's one-line definition appear nowhere in agents/quantify.md or skills/quantify/SKILL.md, and neither file points at the spec; (b) quantify.md:98 lists "measurements, constants (value or range, unit, `per`, `of`, `valid_from`)" as what to harvest from transcripts, which is the numeric reading in writing, and 13/13 stored measurements are transcript-sourced; (c) merge_facts/apply.py:167 skips key derivation when `writes_to.field` is missing, so all 13 slipped through the "verbal report" escape hatch and the canonical `{item}__{record}__{column}` key was never produced once. UI effect, precisely: the 9 numeric entries make `label()` throw on a dev build (factsLabels.ts:789) and render the bare number on a production build; the 4 null ones render an empty label; on all 13 the «زمان · توسط» and «ثبت در» panes are empty.

title: Expressions were dropped, degraded or truncated under validator pressure, leaving unusable rules
description: When the FEEL subset could not express a formula and the validator rejected what was written, the cheapest legal move was to delete or flatten the expression — so 64 computed rules now carry no `expr` at all, 26 were downgraded to a verbatim Google-Sheets formula, and several were rewritten into something semantically wrong. The fallback ('keep the original verbatim') has no completeness guarantee, so five originals are elided with '...' and two are the two-byte string 'JN'. title: Nearly half the store is unreachable: 100 records are plumbing, 268 entries have no inbound reference
description: Walking the reference graph forward from the 139 rules that have inputs reaches 272 of 486 nodes; 214 are unreachable, including 115 records, 59 items, all 22 notes and 13 measurements. Case 2 = WORKBOOK stub: "a Drive id referenced from a formula with no manifest row and no file" — grain:"workbook", key ext_…. Adoption is defined ONLY for case 2. All 30 stubs here are case 1 (they carry location.spreadsheetId + location.sheet, keyed from the dump tab). Zero workbook stubs were minted, so adopted.json==[] and 0/30 grain:"workbook" are the CORRECT expected state, not a failed adoption path.

(2) Root cause refuted by the manifest. attachments/sheets/manifest.json assigns all four stub workbooks to OTHER departments: 1crVTm… "Anbar markazi" → warehouse; 1Te8IM… "Anbar shobe 2" → warehouse; 1AIjH-… "Tedade Fooroosh markazi" → cashier; 10Jsuk… "Tedade Fooroosh naharkhoran" → cashier. Reading the local dump and minting full records would have been a scope violation. The dumps being on disk is irrelevant — the boundary is departmental ownership, not file availability. "A pass that needed a foreign table minted identity rather than reading a file that was already local" is exactly backwards: it minted identity because the spec forbids it from doing anything else.

Edge-kind matrix: nothing anywhere in the store points at a note (0 in-edges of any kind, any source); the only in-edges onto measurements are one mutual pair (F-00300↔F-00301). Notes carry data.about → subject; measurements carry of/per/unit_ref → item. Both kinds are annotation leaves by construction, so "all 22 notes and 13 measurements unreachable" is guaranteed by the data model — a flawless store scores identically. Another 100 of the 214 are the spec-mandated mirror/stub layer (mirrors are required by spec step 2 line ~1442: "a one-formula IMPORT_FROM_SHEET tab gets role: mirror, mirror_of and no fields[]"). title: Scope, coverage and unit claims are asserted beyond the evidence, with no field_status marking the guess
description: Fifty-two items assert both branches while their only source is a chalebagh-branch workbook, and no entry in the store carries a field_status line on scope. Agents also reported negative findings and completeness claims they had not checked, and units were inferred from four sample rows or from column formatting. A factual claim extrapolated from a 4-row sample propagated as a cross_record issue affecting two other batches' entries.
